For an item by store and an item across stores, the average had the lowest error on seven and eight of nine data sets, and the 90% confidence set held a median of 1 and 2 models. For a category by store, a category and the chain total, the lowest-error model differed between data sets and a median of 4 of nine models were not separated by the four to six windows available. For category-by-store planning cost, the average or LightGBM was lowest on seven of eight data sets, and the world model was lowest only on M5; it was behind LightGBM item by store on six of eight. Every trained model used the plan, and on the weekly promotion-driven data pretrained models were less accurate without it. These results hold for these data sets; a forecast solved across all four Ps, or a retailer's own data, may give different results. Every model, test and change that lost is reported.

title: M-JEPA: Predictive Self-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs with Scaffold-Shift Evaluation on Tox21

payload.title: M-JEPA: Predictive Self-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs with Scaffold-Shift Evaluation on Tox21
payload.abstract: Self-supervised molecular representation learning is increasingly used to improve transfer on small, label-limited property prediction tasks, yet commonly used contrastive objectives can be sensitive to view construction and are often evaluated with protocols that report only discrimination. We adapt Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) to molecular graphs by masking chemically coherent connected subgraphs and training a context encoder to regress the masked target embedding produced by an exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher. To evaluate predictive self-supervision under realistic distribution shift, we introduce a leakage-resistant, compute-matched three-phase protocol: (i) an 80-run objective screening on ESOL with fixed compute budgets, (ii) JEPA-only refinement of masking and augmentation choices, and (iii) per-assay Tox21 evaluation under Bemis-Murcko scaffold splits with joint discrimination-reliability analysis and attribution diagnostics. Under matched compute, M-JEPA achieves substantially lower ESOL proxy RMSE than a compute-matched InfoNCE baseline (mean RMSE 2.12 vs 3.75; mean paired dRMSE 1.61; 95% bootstrap CI [1.52, 1.72]; Wilcoxon p=2.4e-4) and typically completes runs faster (~15-25 min vs ~35-45 min on a single GPU under identical hardware), albeit with higher runtime variance. On Tox21, improvements in ROC-AUC/PR-AUC are assay-dependent and do not uniformly imply better calibration; reliability diagrams and Brier/ECE metrics reveal endpoints where fine-tuning improves ranking but leaves probabilities miscalibrated.

title: Spectral Adaptive Graph Transformer for Efficient and Scalable Traffic Forecasting

payload.title: Spectral Adaptive Graph Transformer for Efficient and Scalable Traffic Forecasting
payload.abstract: Traffic forecasting models based on spectral graph convolution offer an interpretable account of how information is mixed between sensors, but they rely on an eigendecomposition of the graph Laplacian. It costs cubic time, is fixed by the road network, and provides a symmetric operator that cannot represent the directed propagation of traffic congestion. Attention-based spatio-temporal transformers remove these limitations but generate a dense sensor-by-sensor attention map at each layer and time step, so memory, rather than accuracy, becomes the binding constraint on large networks. We introduce the spectral adaptive graph transformer, whose spatial operator is learned rather than derived from the Laplacian, directed rather than symmetric, and conditioned on the current traffic state rather than a static state, at a cost linear in the number of sensors. A sparse road graph diffusion branch provides the strictly local propagation that a low-rank operator cannot express, and a zero-initialized gate learns the balance between the two. Before spatial mixing, a unit-mean-gain frequency-bin attention module reweights each sensor's short-term periodicities according to its identity and current context. Across six public benchmarks spanning 170 to 1843 sensors, evaluated over three random seeds, the proposed model attains the lowest error of any single end-to-end model on one benchmark and remains competitive with the strongest current attention models on the others, while using about a quarter of their memory and training about twice as fast.

title: Reflection-Guided Dynamics Rectification for Text-to-Image Generation

payload.title: Reflection-Guided Dynamics Rectification for Text-to-Image Generation
payload.abstract: Fine-grained rectification of existing generations under a limited additional budget remains a key problem in test-time optimization (TTO) for image generation. As for prior approaches, they could identify residual errors, but could not directly ensure that the model acts on the feedback during reasoning. Such errors stem from multiple sources, such as the initial noise or text prompt, and ultimately induce an execution gap of failing to handle potential deviations along the trajectory generating. However, classic models generally cannot remedy this gap. To narrow it, we propose Reflection-Guided Dynamics Rectification (RGDR), which turns reflections on completed outputs into corrective interventions on the process of sampling dynamics at the trajectory level. Specifically, RGDR could impact every sampling step by adapting to instantaneous intervention. Moreover, RGDR generates flexible candidates while adjudicating between them and the reference. As experiments show, rectification from RGDR starts from the existing base trajectory and reflection, and RGDR is substantially more effective than former trajectory exploration. Under matched budgets for additional image generation, RGDR's gain in the cross-model average final checklist score over the reference is $1.51\times$ that of TIR prompt refinement and $1.81\times$ that of Dynamic CFG.

title: HullProbe: Measuring Interventional Part Reliance in Maritime Vessel Classifiers

payload.title: HullProbe: Measuring Interventional Part Reliance in Maritime Vessel Classifiers
payload.abstract: Recognizing a vessel's type from an image supports maritime surveillance and sanctions monitoring, but a classifier can reach high accuracy by leaning on the generic hull instead of the more distinctive superstructure, and is then fooled when a vessel is re-hulled or occluded. De-biasing methods claim to remove such reliance, yet the field certifies them with worst-group accuracy, a proxy that needs group labels and only infers reliance from accuracy. We measure the reliance directly. HullProbe swaps a registered anatomical part of a vessel for another instance's and reads how much that part drives the decision, using a same-class swap to control for compositing artifacts. Because a surface vessel is a hull and a superstructure arranged along one axis, its parts form a 2x3 grid whose 2^6 = 64 swaps we evaluate exhaustively, and a single Walsh transform returns each part's interventional influence and its interaction spectrum. On planted shortcuts, where the true reliance is known, the measure tracks worst-group accuracy (r = -0.94 over 45 configurations), and replacing its learned segmenter with human annotations changes the hull-share by less than the audit's resolution. On the 26 vessel types of MARVEL, the classifier places about 46% of its corrected sensitivity on the generic hull yet follows the superstructure when the two conflict, and the group-label-free de-biasers available there do not detectably reduce the hull's share. The findings hold across three architectures and a second maritime dataset, and the method extends to fine-grained vehicle recognition on Stanford Cars.

title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis

payload.title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis
payload.abstract: Advancing physics reasoning in large language models requires scalable training data that connect physical laws, concrete problem scenarios, and verifiable numerical answers. Expert-designed problems offer top-down control over physical laws, conditions, and scenarios, but require costly human effort. LLM-based synthesis from texts scales efficiently, but model-generated answers and assessments leave supervision vulnerable to hallucinations. We introduce TIRE, a framework for Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution that brings knowledge-driven problem construction to large-scale data generation. Top-down instantiation uses reusable physical formulas and their applicability conditions to control the physical relations and numerical configurations of generated problems. Reliable execution establishes reference answers before problem generation, providing a common numerical foundation for problem construction and teacher distillation. Together, these mechanisms combine control over problem content with execution-grounded supervision for both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Using TIRE, we construct TIRE-19k, spanning nine subfields of physics. Across 3 backbone LLMs and 4 benchmarks, TIRE-19k outperforms 5 representative datasets with equal amounts of SFT data, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.86 percentage points on average. Further GRPO raises Qwen3-8B's average accuracy by 1.52 percentage points over its TIRE-19k SFT checkpoint. These results demonstrate the value of generating physics training data from explicit physical knowledge with reliable execution.

title: Many Repairs, One Direction: Steering Code Models Toward Safer Cryptographic API Use

payload.title: Many Repairs, One Direction: Steering Code Models Toward Safer Cryptographic API Use
payload.abstract: Cryptographic API misuse in large language model-generated code can compromise software security. While many existing approaches improve code security by modifying model parameters or inputs, how representation changes associated with different cryptographic API repairs can support a shared intervention for safer code generation remains underexplored. To investigate this, we construct 48,000 matched program pairs across four programming languages and ten cryptographic API misuse categories. Each pair changes a specified API decision while preserving the programming task. Subtracting the misuse program's internal representation from its secure counterpart's gives a repair vector. Across five models, comparisons of mean repair vectors reveal stronger organization by misuse category than by language. These category-specific patterns also support a shared intervention. We introduce CrypSteer, which extracts a shared direction by normalizing repair differences and selecting a principal component aligned with repairs across misuse categories. With model weights fixed, adding one shared direction per model to its internal activations during generation improves aggregate target security rates by 5.28--15.00 percentage points over unsteered generation across languages and misuse categories. These findings connect the shared structure of cryptographic repair representations to a reusable intervention for safer code generation.

title: Beyond Policy Discrepancy: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

payload.title: Beyond Policy Discrepancy: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
payload.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. We propose Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), which combines specialist merging with capability-guided allocation to account for what the student has already learned. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Supervision decreases as capability gaps close and increases when estimated student capability regresses, while dense token-level guidance remains provided by the teachers. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and instruction following, CA-MOPD achieves an average score of 32.22, outperforming naive MOPD, Open-MOPD, and the merged initialization by 0.86, 0.83, and 0.74 points, respectively. Controlled comparisons further support the benefits of merged initialization and capability-gap guidance under matched training budgets.

title: LC-TSRNet: A Land-Cover-Guided Two-Stage Network for Annual MODIS Surface Reflectance Time Series Reconstruction

payload.title: LC-TSRNet: A Land-Cover-Guided Two-Stage Network for Annual MODIS Surface Reflectance Time Series Reconstruction
payload.abstract: MODIS surface reflectance (SR) products often suffer from data gaps due to cloud contamination and sensor malfunctions, limiting their applications in long-term and large-scale studies. Most existing methods rely on cloud-free observations from optical time series or introduce SAR time series as auxiliary information. However, due to the coarse spatial resolution of MODIS, cloud-free reference images are difficult to obtain, and SAR imagery is not well matched to the spatial resolution of MODIS, making it difficult to provide effective prior constraints. To address these issues, this study proposes LC-TSRNet for seamless reconstruction of annual MODIS SR products. In the first stage, an annual land cover map is introduced as prior knowledge, and CSPM is designed by leveraging the spectral similarity within identical land cover types, thereby providing prior spectral constraints for missing regions. In the second stage, to address large-area, persistent, and overlapping gaps in MODIS imagery, SMRM is designed to adaptively exploit and integrate multi-scale spatiotemporal contextual information. Meanwhile, to address the limited collaborative utilization of spatio-temporal-spectral information, 3DAM is designed to impose cross-dimensional joint constraints. Considering the lack of publicly available MODIS sample datasets, this study constructs the AIRMOD-TSR dataset. Extensive experimental results show that LC-TSRNet outperforms the comparison methods and achieves better reconstruction accuracy and spectral fidelity. Under the spatially adjacent scenario, LC-TSRNet improves PSNR by 0.56 dB and reduces SAM by 0.13°. The vegetation monitoring application further verifies the practical value of the reconstructed SR time series.

title: Compile Once, Run Cheap: Frozen, Portable Skills for Embodied Agents, and What Recursive Self-Improvement Adds

payload.title: Compile Once, Run Cheap: Frozen, Portable Skills for Embodied Agents, and What Recursive Self-Improvement Adds
payload.abstract: Embodied AI lacks the data-rich pretraining that gave language models their agents and skills, so new manipulation capability costs demonstrations per task or a frontier model in every episode. We study a third route: a strong general model acts only as an offline author that writes, runs, diagnoses and repairs a manipulation skill in simulation until it passes an exam on layouts drawn after freezing; the frozen skill then runs as code alone or under a cheap caller that reads only its description. We call this skill-level recursive self-improvement Skill-RSI and specify a compile protocol (isolated, audited author; hidden validation layouts; no-feedback and inherit-only controls; tamper-evident ledger) and a reuse protocol that runs the identical files with executors from another model family. On 7 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with cluttered tables, Claude Code compiled 4 tasks into 7 frozen skills, 5 from a first draft needing only qualification, at USD 4.29-8.22 of author cost each (USD 55 per skill counting the 13 failed campaigns). The other three tasks did not compile in 18 campaigns, including five with GPT-6 and a pre-registered 150-layout run: on the hardest task every campaign scored 78-95 of 100 but had 3-16 safety aborts, failing the gate of 95% success with zero aborts; a 100-episode exam bounds an abort rate only to 3.6%. On hidden layouts, repair that inherits the previous version beat from-scratch rewriting in 8 of 8 controlled campaigns (sign test p = 0.004); an inherit-only lineage attributes most of the gap to inheritance, with development feedback adding a little (3 of 3, p = 0.125). Write-once campaigns found no detectable first-draft effect of practice (minimum detectable effect 14 points). The frozen skills kept 148/150 successes on new layouts with no model and 147/150 with a DeepSeek-flash caller at USD 0.00028-0.00054 per episode; no direct-control baseline was run.

title: A learner-free swarm reaches the explore-exploit equilibrium: A self-organized attractor approximating the reinforcement-learning solution

payload.title: A learner-free swarm reaches the explore-exploit equilibrium: A self-organized attractor approximating the reinforcement-learning solution
payload.abstract: The explore-exploit trade-off is the core problem of reinforcement learning (RL). In its multi-agent, resource-sharing form the optimum is not a scalar-return maximum but an equilibrium allocation -- the ideal-free distribution (IFD), the Nash equilibrium of a congestion game. We show that a minimal foraging swarm reaches the shape of this equilibrium as a self-organized attractor -- foragers in proportion to resource richness (matching slope 0.94) -- with no learner, no trained parameters, and no payoff or reward read anywhere in its dynamics. Agents explore by heavy-tailed (Levy) flights, recruit neighbours to a discovery through a threshold cascade on their proximity network, and disperse as a patch crowds; removing the coupling of recruitment to movement collapses the matching (slope 0.08). The reinforcement learning is at the level of the problem and the allocation reached, not the micro-rule. The swarm reaches this equilibrium rather than learning it, attaining its shape but not the exact equilibrium: it stays measurably exploitable (Nash-gap 0.58 versus ~0.01 for a converged learner). Against PPO learners (feedforward, centralized-critic, and graph message-passing) trained in the same sensing-limited environment, the reward-free swarm at zero training matches the IFD gradient more faithfully than any learner (slope ~1 vs 0.69-0.91) and ties the best learner's harvest where clustered (both plateau at ~0.80 of an oracle ceiling), while the learner collects more where resource is scarce (0.33 vs 0.22) and holds tighter per-capita intake. Learning thus buys precision and transfer, not a better allocation; neither message passing nor a centralized critic exceeds it at this budget. We read this not as beating RL, but as evidence that a minimal swarm's physics reaches the equilibrium RL seeks without a learner, a reward, or a trained parameter. A companion paper develops the mechanism.

title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D

payload.title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D
payload.abstract: Despite having an asymptotically optimal rate of convergence on convex quadratics, the acceleration of Polyak's heavy-ball method and a characterization of its dynamics within more general settings have remained long standing open problems. Recently, the work of Goujaud et al. [Math. Program. (2025)] made progress regarding acceleration in the context of smooth, strongly convex minimization: for a small enough inverse condition number, either the method does not accelerate on quadratics, or there exists a smooth strongly convex function such that heavy-ball cycles over the roots of unity. The constructed functions have two variables, thus leaving the question of acceleration over univariate functions open. In this work, we use a Fourier-based analysis to i) provide a proof for the non-acceleration of the heavy-ball method over the class of univariate smooth strongly convex functions. We also ii) provide a strict enlargement of the previous root-of-unity cycling region, with insights regarding the "fractional" sets of Goujaud et al. [arXiv:2502.19916], and iii) give a higher dimensional cycling instance which is not covered by root-of-unity cycling.

title: Pre-Query Retention with Bounded Bit and Word Retrieval

payload.title: Pre-Query Retention with Bounded Bit and Word Retrieval
payload.abstract: An agent can retain information before receiving a future question and later retrieve evidence from an archive. Evaluating this arrangement requires accounting for both retained information and the width of each retrieval response. Decision-tree capacity bounds describe individual sets of distinguishable records, but a memory writer must encode every possible record before the query is known. We study fixed-length retention beside an immutable binary archive, with a worst-case limit on raw bit or word reads. We characterize feasible one-bit-read memory cells and construct encoders that partition the complete record space. Supporting pairwise exclusive disjunction and conjunction with one bit read is equivalent to supporting every Boolean query. For multiple reads, we combine explicit encoders with decision-tree counting and an entropy converse. The word-read bounds differ by at most two retained bits when the read budget is at most half the archive length. Under an explicit condition on word width and archive length, raw-word caching attains the exact optimum among all writers. A related condition preserves this optimum under positive average error. Exhaustive checks validate the implementations. In a matched dialogue-agent study, a categorical sufficient statistic preserves source decisions with less storage and lower decoding latency than the universal encoder. A catalogue-specific index reduces private state further and requires additional shared storage. The results characterize how response width and future query structure determine retention requirements.

title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources

payload.title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources
payload.abstract: Enterprise retail workflows require agents to chain evidence across heterogeneous sources, from structured product and order records to unstructured inquiries and reviews, yet existing agentic RAG benchmarks rarely capture this challenge. To enable controlled evaluation of such workflows, we introduce RetailBridge, a compositional retail benchmark built from persona-driven simulations. Its questions are constructed by linking entities and intermediate answers across heterogeneous sources, requiring agents to identify the relevant sources, carry evidence between them, and produce a grounded answer. To systematically evaluate LLMs on these retail workflows, we develop RetailRAG, a retail-aware framework equipped with auto-schema briefing, source-routed plan chaining, and diagnostic plan revision. RetailRAG consistently outperforms existing agentic RAG baselines across all evaluation axes, serving as a strong reference system for assessing LLM agents on retail workflows. On RetailBridge, evaluating ten LLM backbones with RetailRAG reveals multi-source chaining as the dominant bottleneck across providers and model scales, suggesting that reliable retail agents require explicit cross-source orchestration rather than scaling alone. Code and data are publicly available at \url{https://github.com/DISL-Lab/RetailBridge}.

title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?

payload.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
payload.abstract: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution.

title: Localization and Neural Splatting on the Edge: An FPGA Scene Memory for Robots

payload.title: Localization and Neural Splatting on the Edge: An FPGA Scene Memory for Robots
payload.abstract: Resource-constrained robots and autonomous vehicles need scene memories that localize a camera and render nearby views without a desktop GPU. Scene-coordinate regression (SCR) and 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) fit because they avoid an SfM stage, but ACEsplat-style pipelines are GPU-centered, and moving them to an edge FPGA is hard because SCR is pose-sensitive and 3DGS rendering is irregular and capacity-sensitive. We present LENS, an edge scene-memory acceleration system on the AMD KR260 that brings an ACEsplat-style workload to a low-power FPGA/ARM platform. Rather than proposing a new scene model, LENS co-designs the two dominant kernels with the board data path: an INT16 SCR accelerator that preserves pose accuracy, and a bit-exact fixed-point ordered 3DGS renderer that rewrites alpha transmittance as a log-sum-exp recurrence and removes provably useless streamed Gaussians. All LENS latency, power, and quality results are board-measured. The SCR engine preserves DSAC* localization accuracy at 25.42 ms, the on-board renderer reaches 34.11 dB on Cambridge against ACEsplat's 33.20, novel-view synthesis on RealEstate10K reaches 27.84 dB against 26.11, and all ten Wayspots scenes reach the ACEsplat rendering target. LENS wins performance per watt over a Jetson Orin NX on every deployment task, by 1.9x to 5.7x at about a quarter of the power, and is faster in absolute latency on localization and Wayspots rendering. On-device training reaches ACEsplat-level quality but not the GPU's time or energy, marking the remaining boundary for a future training accelerator.

title: One Skill Takes Over: Clashing Agent Skills and a One-File Fix

payload.title: One Skill Takes Over: Clashing Agent Skills and a One-File Fix
payload.abstract: Agent Skills are instruction files that tell a coding agent how to do one job. Users install skills from many authors, so two skills for the same job can be active at the same time. We ask what a model does when both skill files are in its context: does it combine their compatible rules, or follow one skill and drop the other? We build SkillClash, 16 pairs of same-job skills in which code checks every rule and a reference output shows the best result that can be reached. On seven models from five families, from 4B open models to Qwen3-235B and GPT-4.1, a skill's rules are followed 93 to 99% of the time when it is loaded alone and 61 to 62% when a same-job skill is loaded next to it. Most outputs show takeover: every rule that only one skill asks for is followed, and every rule that only the other skill asks for is dropped. The worked examples inside the skills drive this. When each skill file instead ends with one example that follows both skills, takeover falls to 1 to 15% on the six models we tested. Telling the model which skill has priority does not bring the dropped skill back, and telling it to apply both skills brings the dropped skill back only on the two strong models and leaves the interacting rules broken. One merged skill file written by the strongest model we used, Claude Opus 5.5, lets all seven models follow 96 to 99% of the achievable rules. Most of its gain over a plain list of both skills' rules comes from its one worked example, and such an example helps only when it is correct. Code and data: https://github.com/prazmara/skillclash

title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System

payload.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
payload.abstract: Conversational recommender systems have recently adopted vision-language models to match user dialogue intents with multimodal product information. However, extending these methods to many product domains faces a dilemma: deploying a separately adapted VLM per domain scales cost linearly with the number of domains and requires routing each dialogue to the right model, while naively merging all domains into a single VLM degrades accuracy because product characteristics vary widely across categories. We propose LightCRS, a lightweight, query-conditioned framework for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. LightCRS precomputes multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. Online, a compact 5.3M-parameter module fuses this evidence for each dialogue via query-conditioned cross-attention, whose parameters are shared across all domains, and compares candidates jointly with an inter-candidate Transformer. To enable rigorous evaluation, we construct MM-R2A-25, a 25-domain benchmark pairing natural Reddit recommendation-seeking conversations with Amazon product listings. LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art average HR@1, NDCG@5, and MRR, improving HR@1 by 35.4\% over the strongest baseline while reducing per-query latency by 266 times. Joint multi-domain training itself improves HR@1 by 15.2\% over separately trained single-domain models.

title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Pointwise Replicable Agnostic Learning

payload.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Pointwise Replicable Agnostic Learning
payload.abstract: Pointwise replicability asks that two independently trained predictors, using the same random seed, agree at each fixed query with high probability. We determine its optimal agnostic sample complexity on finite and countable domains. For every nonempty binary class of finite VC dimension $d\ge1$, the required number of independent examples is $Θ\!\left(\frac{d}{ρ^2α^2}+\frac{\log(1/β)}{α^2}\right)$, uniformly over independent accuracy, failure, and disagreement parameters $α,β,ρ\in(0,1/10)$. The learner returns one binary function, may be improper, and uses unrestricted shared randomness. Its sample budget is fixed before observing data, and the replicability guarantee includes queries of zero marginal mass. The main construction combines an ensemble of empirical-risk minimizers with a smooth, signal-dependent risk decomposition. A single shared phase selects the final binary predictor. Record times certify its weak-signal risk, while a uniform bound protects the strong-signal risk at that same selected time. A phase-comparison theorem controls the actual shared-seed execution under simultaneous changes in the marginals and risk coefficients. A rare repair step then makes the confidence cost additive. Together with matching lower bounds, this removes the remaining logarithmic overhead and parameter restrictions in the general countable-domain sample-complexity problem. This extended version also retains the earlier explicit constructions and their proofs, including proper learning for VC-one classes, the full finite-atom class, a faster realizable bound, and counterexamples that separate restrictions of particular algorithms from restrictions of the learning problem.

title: Normalizing Flow for Neural-Enhanced Track-Before-Detect

payload.title: Normalizing Flow for Neural-Enhanced Track-Before-Detect
payload.abstract: Multiobject tracking (MOT) is a fundamental capability in autonomous navigation, radar and sonar systems, as well as 6G integrated sensing-and-communication (ISAC) networks. In this paper, we propose a neural-enhanced track-before-detect (TkBD) framework that operates directly on complex-valued raw signals and learns a latent representation of unmodeled propagation effects during runtime. We introduce an environment-dependent latent intensity variable that characterizes the signal power of each object in the shared propagation environment. The probability density function of this intensity variable is represented by a normalizing flow and trained online in an unsupervised manner within the sequential Bayesian inference procedure. The learning objective is derived from a variational Bayes formulation by maximizing the evidence lower bound (ELBO), thereby accounting for the uncertainties inherent in the Bayesian TkBD problem. To enable scalable inference, we make use of a recently introduced Bayesian TkBD framework that combines belief propagation, which avoids high-dimensional operations, with sequential Monte Carlo methods for efficient low-dimensional updates.

title: Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation

payload.title: Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation
payload.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains agents on their own trajectories using supervision from a stronger teacher. We uncover a counterintuitive phenomenon in multi-turn agentic tasks: a smaller, initially weaker student can substantially outperform its teacher during training, only to regress as distillation continues. We term this phenomenon distillation overshoot. Through decision- and task-level analyses, we trace overshoot to two competing effects of OPD: repairing weak student decisions and eroding successful student choices that the teacher disfavors. Early in training, repair outpaces erosion, allowing the student to combine the teacher's corrections with its own strengths and surpass the teacher. As training continues, erosion overtakes repair, causing these gains to vanish. Motivated by this finding, we propose Success-Preserving On-Policy Distillation (SPOD), which selectively masks conflicting teacher supervision on successful student choices and introduces a soft probability floor to counteract their erosion, while retaining teacher guidance elsewhere. SPOD requires only binary episode success and model probabilities already available during OPD. Across two model families and three agentic benchmarks, SPOD consistently outperforms ordinary OPD and evaluated variants, improving final success by up to 15.2 percentage points and surpassing the teacher by up to 20.0 points. Moreover, SPOD's final checkpoints outperform even ordinary OPD's best intermediate checkpoints in all six settings, demonstrating that beyond-teacher gains can be not only preserved but further extended. Code: https://github.com/Jike338/SPOD

title: Strictly Replicable Realizable Learning: Unknown Marginals, Finite-Class Interpolation, and the Cost of Shared Randomness

payload.title: Strictly Replicable Realizable Learning: Unknown Marginals, Finite-Class Interpolation, and the Cost of Shared Randomness
payload.abstract: Strict replicability requires two independent training samples, processed with the same random seed, to produce exactly the same hypothesis. We study realizable Boolean learning under unknown and known instance marginals. For unknown marginals, we obtain the worst-case sample complexity $Θ(((\log M)^2/ρ^2+\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon)$ for classes of cardinality at most $M$, throughout a fixed small-parameter range. This resolves the distribution-free finite-class sample-complexity question up to universal constants and rules out a general $ρ^{-1}$ dependence. The upper bound uses a truncated-power distribution with a hard empirical-error budget. For known marginals, a control-variate learner uses $O(((1+\log M)^{3/2}/ρ+\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon)$ samples, and explicit uniform-marginal instances establish the matching class-size exponent. On a product of $d$ finite threshold chains of length $k$, we determine the exact rate $Θ((dk\log(1+\sqrt d/(kρ))+\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon)$. We also characterize deterministic learning, the very-small-$ρ$ regime for arbitrary finite classes, and every cardinality-replicability regime for finite classes of VC dimension one. A VC-covering-number bound yields the fixed-accuracy exponent $3/2$ independently of cardinality. Finally, we separate statistical complexity from implementation costs: we prove a sharp fixed-block trade-off, short-seed existence bounds, and a shared rejection-filter reduction from optimal learning of the full Boolean class to efficient public sampling of ordinary Bernoulli product distributions. Detailed proofs include the geometric lower bounds, the discrete posterior-kernel comparison, and the finite-bit constructions.

title: Synergy-Aware Residual Flow Matching for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

payload.title: Synergy-Aware Residual Flow Matching for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
payload.abstract: Predicting single-cell responses to genetic and chemical perturbations is important for understanding regulatory mechanisms and prioritizing therapeutic interventions. Existing methods have made progress by modeling perturbation-conditioned expression shifts with neural networks, graph priors, foundation-model representations, or distributional generative models. However, combinatorial perturbation prediction remains challenging because much of the response can be explained by additive single-perturbation effects, while the biologically informative signal often lies in a smaller non-additive residual induced by perturbation interactions. Directly generating the full post-perturbation expression profile may therefore allocate substantial capacity to the dominant additive component and underemphasize synergy-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{SynGeneFlow}, a synergy-aware flow matching framework that anchors the source distribution at an additive prior and learns a residual flow toward the true perturbed state. SynGeneFlow further incorporates perturbation-conditioned gene interaction modeling, where a static gene-gene mask provides biological structure and a perturbation-dependent deformation bias dynamically modulates gene-gene coupling. To preserve population-level response structure, we align both endpoint distributions and biological residual distributions with MMD-based regularization. We evaluate SynGeneFlow on genetic and drug perturbation benchmarks under observed-single, held-out, and cross-modality settings. The results demonstrate that residualizing flow matching around additive perturbation effects provides a biologically grounded and robust framework for single-cell perturbation response prediction.

title: LLM Agents as Suppliers of Physical System Models: Calibration and Acceptance in Modelica

payload.title: LLM Agents as Suppliers of Physical System Models: Calibration and Acceptance in Modelica
payload.abstract: To procure a model of a device, a client hands a supplier a description, sometimes with recorded data or a target response, and accepts the model against this handover. We let LLM coding agents act as the supplier on handovers with data, building Modelica models from library components for four simulated systems and a real switching magnet, and ask what acceptance certifies. Several agents reach the noise floor, but a handover admits a set of models: the description leaves parts of the structure open, and the data narrow it only to the agreed accuracy. We therefore accept by membership in this set, not by matching one reference, and add layers above behaviour: a physical invariant exposes an energy-creating model at the noise floor. Interpretability becomes a property of the delivered model, tested on a variant, read where none exists and shaped through the handover. Most failures are fits delivered with a systematic residual on their own fitting data, where the handover left open how close is close enough. In a follow-up, stating a threshold makes the agents compare against it, and more deliveries pass. The argument applies wherever a handover underspecifies a model meant to be read, not only run.

title: Decentralized Online Exp-Concave Optimization

payload.title: Decentralized Online Exp-Concave Optimization
payload.abstract: Decentralized Online Convex Optimization (D-OCO) is a fundamental framework in which a set of local agents aims to minimize a sequence of global loss functions using only local computations and communications. While recent work has established near-optimal regret guarantees for convex and strongly convex losses, the case of exp-concave losses remains an open challenge: specifically, whether logarithmic regret is achievable. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively by proposing Decentralized Online Newton Step (D-ONS), which adapts the idea of blocking and accelerated gossip to the Online Newton Step algorithm in a non-trivial manner. Concretely, our algorithm achieves a regret bound of $O\left(Nd(1-σ_2)^{-1/2}\,\log^2(T) \right)$ where $N$ is the number of agents, $d$ is the dimension, $T$ is the horizon, and $1-σ_2$ represents the spectral gap of the network. To our knowledge, this is the first logarithmic regret bound for decentralized online exp-concave optimization. We further establish a nearly matching lower bound of $Ω\left(Nd (1-σ_2)^{-1/2}\,\log(T/N) \right)$ showing the near optimality of our upper bound. Finally, we extend our algorithm to decentralized online linear regression in which the feasible domain is unbounded and features and labels are locally observed. By gossiping covariance and label-feature statistics, we also achieve logarithmic regret.

title: Multifidelity Monte Carlo Estimator for High-Dimensional Quantities of Interest

payload.title: Multifidelity Monte Carlo Estimator for High-Dimensional Quantities of Interest
payload.abstract: Multifidelity Monte Carlo (MFMC) reduces the cost of estimating the statistics of quantities of interest (QoIs) computed via expensive high-fidelity model by using cheaper low-fidelity models as control variates. We extend MFMC to vector-valued QoIs by replacing the scalar control-variate coefficients with matrices and minimizing a weighted mean-squared error. The optimal full-matrix coefficients are available in closed form, and their variance reduction is summarized by an effective correlation that takes the place of the squared Pearson correlation in the closed-form MFMC design. Restricting the coefficients to block-diagonal, diagonal, and scalar classes gives a nested hierarchy of estimators with increasing variance reduction and increasing pilot-data demand, with closed-form coefficients for compatible weightings. For a scalar QoI obtained by linearly projecting the state, correcting the full state before projecting is never worse at the population level. Experiments on a Gaussian problem, a reduced-order model of an advection--diffusion problem, and a coarse-grid two-phase flow problem show that the best class depends on the pilot size relative to the number of covariance quantities it must estimate, and that reusing the pilot samples lowers the mean-squared error.

title: Conjugate Compilation: Self-Improving Agentic Co-Compilation for Speculative Decoding

payload.title: Conjugate Compilation: Self-Improving Agentic Co-Compilation for Speculative Decoding
payload.abstract: As LLM adoption surges, scaling model serving requires unlocking stranded GPU capacity alongside deploying more GPUs. Speculative decoding brings two models into the serving process: a small draft model proposes tokens that a larger target model verifies. Yet compiling these models individually leaves their shared execution outside the compiler's optimization boundary. We introduce CONJUGATE COMPILATION, which reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem and jointly optimizes the draft and target models within their shared execution rather than treating each in isolation. Our key insight is that cross-model compilation should be informed by the measured performance of the co-located shared execution it produces: an optimization that improves a kernel in isolation need not improve the models when they execute together. To expand cross-model opportunities, we devise operand layouts that interleave blocks from both models within common tiles, co-locating GEMM and non-GEMM work while preserving their mathematics. We realize CONJUGATE COMPILATION through a self-improving agentic search system in which an LLM edits cross-model optimization plans using the compiler and GPU execution as its environment. Each proposed plan is compiled and evaluated through its co-located shared execution, whose measured score, together with kernel-level verdicts and compiler feedback, informs subsequent proposals, while Monte Carlo tree search accumulates rewards to guide exploration. Across six single-GPU speculative-decoding configurations on NVIDIA B300 and RTX 5090 GPUs, CONJUGATE COMPILATION achieves a geometric-mean per-round speedup of 1.37x over conventional execution. Interleaved kernels raise this speedup to 1.45x, reaching 1.59x in the best case. CONJUGATE COMPILATION also improves GPU utilization on average by 1.46x on RTX 5090 and 1.50x on B300.

title: FineSplat: Fine Patches, Local Groups, Detailed Splats

payload.title: FineSplat: Fine Patches, Local Groups, Detailed Splats
payload.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) promises instant scene reconstruction with high-quality novel-view synthesis. Yet, fine-grained geometry and appearance remain difficult to recover, motivating us to revisit how feed-forward models represent, aggregate, and refine detailed visual information. We introduce FineSplat, a feed-forward 3DGS framework built around fine-grained image patches. Since global multi-view attention becomes prohibitively expensive at such high token resolutions, we develop a dual-grouping strategy that combines two complementary forms of locality: view-wise grouping enables efficient interaction among neighboring views, while 3D spatial grouping reconnects geometrically related tokens that may never have interacted under view-wise grouping by lifting them into the 3D scene space. We further leverage reconstruction error as direct feedback, providing an explicit rendering-based signal to recover fine-grained structures and appearance, thereby overcoming the limitations of one-pass feed-forward prediction. Finally, a compact Gaussian generation scheme preserves the benefits of fine-grained features without unnecessarily increasing the number of primitives. Together, these designs enable FineSplat to recover richer geometry and appearance while remaining efficient and compact, achieving state-of-the-art results by a substantial margin, under the same or smaller Gaussian budgets than existing methods.

title: No Escape from the Quadratic Barrier: Adaptive Attacks on Linear $\ell_2$ Sketches

payload.title: No Escape from the Quadratic Barrier: Adaptive Attacks on Linear $\ell_2$ Sketches
payload.abstract: Linear sketches estimate properties of high-dimensional inputs from a fixed low-dimensional projection. At constant accuracy, randomized Euclidean-norm sketches, notably the Johnson-Lindenstrauss transform, support exponentially many nonadaptive queries in sketch dimension $k$. For adaptive black-box queries, known privacy-based defenses guarantee $\widetildeΩ(k^2)$ and it remained open whether stronger guarantees were possible. Prior attacks used more queries, restricted the responder, or provided weaker failure guarantees. We show that the quadratic guarantee is optimal up to logarithmic factors, even with a computationally unbounded responder that knows the matrix, attack algorithm, history, and query distributions and may change its randomized rule after every query. For every fixed hidden $A\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times n}$ with $n>40k$ and target accuracy $α\in (0,1]$, our black-box attack uses $O(k+α^2k^2\log(2+α^2k))$ queries in $\widetilde{O}(1+α^2k)$ adaptive rounds to force, with constant probability, a round in which a constant fraction of answers have $Ω(α)$ relative error. Our results clarify the limits of defending a fixed compressive linear representation by adapting the prediction rule.

title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4

payload.title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4
payload.abstract: Automated theorem provers often rely on sampling language models, but proof assistants like Lean reject each failed step with a precise error message --- information that pure sampling discards. To overcome this, we introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module. Our search samples $K$ candidate tactics at each step and repairs a failed tactic at most $R$ times. Instead of discarding failed tactics, we feed the compiler's error message to a pretrained repair model to fix individual rejected steps in place. This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark. Repair is not free: it trades extra runtime for reachable proofs. But the trade is predictable: repair pays most when sampling is constrained; its return is front-loaded, with the first repair attempt capturing $84\text{--}96\%$ of the total gain; and the gain comes almost entirely from shallow tactic-execution failures rather than structural errors such as type mismatches. This targeted repair successfully replicates on a second benchmark (Lean Workbook), nearly doubling the solve rate with zero regressions.

title: UpLoop: Upcycling Large Language Models with Gated Loop

payload.title: UpLoop: Upcycling Large Language Models with Gated Loop
payload.abstract: Looped large language models trade parameter storage for recurrent computation, but most are trained from scratch. In practice, pretraining with looped depth is expensive, making post-training upcycling of a pretrained non-looped LLM an attractive alternative. We introduce \textbf{UpLoop}, a post-training recipe based on \emph{layer-wise} recurrence. Instead of looping a whole model or a middle block, UpLoop loops each selected layer locally, preserving the pretrained depth hierarchy and avoiding feature-space mismatch. To make loop execution useful, we add hidden-wise gates on the attention and MLP residual branches, so later loops act as progressive refinements rather than redundant rewrites. Empirically, UpLoop breaks the commonly observed saturation at two loops ($R=2$) in prior looped models. Starting from Qwen3-4B Base and applying SFT, UpLoop improves the average accuracy across 20 benchmarks by 6.17\% at $R=3$. We use $R=3$ as the main setting for the best accuracy--cost trade-off, while both native and extrapolated $R=4$ yield further gains.

title: UtoMe: Observation-Uncertainty-Guided Token Merging for Weather Foundation Models

payload.title: UtoMe: Observation-Uncertainty-Guided Token Merging for Weather Foundation Models
payload.abstract: Weather transformers process dense reanalysis fields whose reliability varies across variables, locations, and weather regimes. Token merging can reduce computation, but feature similarity alone does not account for this heterogeneous input uncertainty. We introduce UtoMe, an observation-uncertainty-guided token merging framework that combines dynamics saliency with ensemble data assimilation spread as a relative input-reliability proxy. The resulting importance score protects selected tokens as anchors and calibrates bipartite matching between the remaining tokens. Three variants use external uncertainty at both training and inference, during training only, or neither stage. In ERA5 72-hour forecasting at two spatial resolutions, UtoMe improves Overall error over train-time ToMe at matched token budgets. At $1.40625^\circ$ and 50% token reduction, UtoMe-E lowers Overall error from 67.32 to 53.00 at the same 0.55x encoder FLOPs. Small reductions remain close to the full-token baseline; larger reductions incur measurable accuracy losses. Component ablations and spatial uncertainty controls support combining dynamics with aligned uncertainty when allocating a weather transformer's token budget.

title: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing the Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space

payload.title: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing the Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space
payload.abstract: Prompt injection is the dominant security risk for large-language-model (LLM) applications and agents, yet the field still lacks a coherent map of how these attacks are constructed. More than twenty public datasets describe prompt injection using incompatible vocabularies, often organized around delivery vector, attacker goal, or generation method. In this Systematization of Knowledge, we present PIAtlas, a taxonomy organized instead around how the injected instruction is constructed to subvert the underlying model. Its six classes, one per subversion mechanism, form the roots of a hierarchy of techniques and sub-techniques that researchers can use to describe attacks consistently and design more systematic evaluations. We derive the taxonomy from how LLMs are trained, prompted, and influenced by human-like framing, and compare it with historical attack data. To ground this comparison, we release PICorpus, to our knowledge the largest license-clean collection of public prompt-injection datasets, and map thousands of its records to PIAtlas under a human-verified protocol. The mapping shows that attacks usually combine several techniques drawn from only a few mechanisms. It also reveals gaps that existing labels obscure: widely used agent benchmarks test only part of the attack space, and adaptive attackers favor mechanisms that curated benchmarks underrepresent. PIAtlas thus provides a common foundation for understanding this attack space, improving benchmark coverage, and guiding red teaming and defenses.

title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing

payload.title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
payload.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are enabling agents to move beyond predefined workflows toward autonomous planning and execution, creating new opportunities for smart manufacturing. However, dynamic environments, complex physical constraints, and stringent reliability requirements hinder the direct deployment of general-purpose agents in smart manufacturing. This article presents a systematic overview of LLM-driven industrial agents. First, we analyze five key challenges and discuss the concept and core characteristics of industrial agents. We then establish a unified taxonomy covering application scenarios, embodiment forms, and five capability levels. Next, we propose a four-layer system architecture and detail its core modules and operational mechanisms for closed-loop task execution. Finally, we review representative applications across the industrial lifecycle and outline future research directions. This article provides a structured reference for the design, development, and application of industrial agents.

title: MultiAltitudeSR: Multi-Altitude Agricultural UAV Image Super-Resolution via Physical Ground Sampling Distance Conditioning

payload.title: MultiAltitudeSR: Multi-Altitude Agricultural UAV Image Super-Resolution via Physical Ground Sampling Distance Conditioning
payload.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) enable high-throughput platforms for crop monitoring but face a fundamental trade-off between flight altitude and image spatial resolution. Many existing super-resolution (SR) methods for UAV imagery rely on oversimplified synthetic degradation models and are restricted to fixed integer upsampling scales, limiting their ability to handle real-world degradations and varying flight altitudes. This study proposes MultiAltitudeSR, a framework that conditions feature modulation and reconstruction on source and target ground sampling distances (GSDs). MultiAltitudeSR trained jointly on real UAV images at altitudes of 10 to 70 m above ground level supports all 21 source-to-target altitude pairs without pair-specific fine-tuning, covering scale factors ranging from 1.18$\times$ to 6.03$\times$. The framework can be extended to additional source-target GSD combinations by incorporating corresponding image pairs into training. On the 20-to-10 m pair, the model achieved competitive perceptual performance compared with pair-specific baselines, with LPIPS of 0.2236, DISTS of 0.2431, and NIQE of 8.9020. Experiments using the same architecture demonstrated the value of acquiring real-world multi-altitude UAV image pairs for SR training, with real-pair training achieving better average reconstruction performance across the 21 altitude pairs than training with the tested synthetic degradation pipeline. Downstream zero-shot segmentation case studies illustrated task-dependent benefits of super-resolved imagery for crop monitoring, suggesting potential UAV flight-time savings through image acquisition at higher altitudes.

title: CorrectRTL: Boost RTL Generation Quality Through Automated Self-Correction with Instruction Decomposition

payload.title: CorrectRTL: Boost RTL Generation Quality Through Automated Self-Correction with Instruction Decomposition
payload.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong promise in specification-to-RTL generation. Among the explorations, the self-correction paradigm has significantly advanced LLM-based RTL generation. However, two challenges limit further progress. Existing benchmarks are saturated by advanced LLMs, leaving little room to evaluate the agentic self-correction framework. The monolithic self-correction paradigm rewrites the entire design at once, where LLMs are susceptible to error confusion and corruption of originally correct code. To address the benchmark challenge, we contribute ScaleBench, a more challenging benchmark of 200 complex RTL designs. To address the challenge in methodology, we propose CorrectRTL, an agentic framework that realizes a new decompose-then-correct paradigm, in which the LLM agent explicitly decouples scaffold construction from detailed implementation. CorrectRTL contributes three core techniques: (1)~\emph{Structure-oriented decomposition}, (2)~\emph{Snippet-based RAG}, and (3)~\emph{SVA-based self-correction}. On ScaleBench, CorrectRTL improves Pass@1 from 20.5% to 49.0% (+28.5%). On VerilogEval, CorrectRTL achieves up to 96.1% Pass@1, demonstrating consistent improvements across both simple and complex designs.

title: Towards Human-AI Complementarity for AI Safety

payload.title: Towards Human-AI Complementarity for AI Safety
payload.abstract: Safely overseeing AI is increasingly challenging for the humans doing it, as they must evaluate longer and more complex outputs with every new model generation. To mitigate this challenge, we could leverage complementarity: where humans and models make different mistakes, combining their judgements could yield an oversight signal stronger than either produces alone. We study this opportunity in realistic, safety-relevant settings, contributing the largest known suite of such tasks (3,957 instances across 8 datasets and 6 domains) as well as a platform and data pipeline for measuring human, AI, and human-AI performance on matched items. We collected 35,613 judgements from 416 human raters, finding a considerable opportunity for a complementarity effect. We also found that with the assistance methods we tested, human raters corrected the AI's errors less often, even when overall human accuracy rose, and the hybridisation methods we tested added little over the better single source on average. While complementarity is an important and feasible engineering target for safe oversight, achieving it remains an open challenge for future work.

title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents

payload.title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
payload.abstract: AI coworkers must coordinate tools, communicate across turns, and act on changing workspace state while respecting workflow constraints. Constructing training experience for these capabilities requires coherent requests, service records, tool interfaces, and grading checks. We present CoworkEnv, a capability-guided framework for synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworkers. Workflow requirements guide task construction, and programmatic validation with feedback repair checks generated specifications and grading behavior. Teacher executions yield curated demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while student interactions provide rollouts and rewards for reinforcement learning (RL). Using these resources, we train compact PocketWorker models. For Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, SFT raises the mean score from 46.6 to 64.1 on Claw-Eval, including a 31.9-point gain on Multi-turn tasks. An SFT-only extension to ClawMark demonstrates applicability across coworker benchmarks. We further compare RL training dynamics across configurations that vary reward processing and credit assignment. Improving training rewards provide preliminary evidence that the constructed environments support policy optimization.

title: MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents

payload.title: MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents
payload.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents face a fundamental allocation problem as interaction histories grow: which information to retain, how much context to devote to it, and at what granularity. Existing memory mechanisms largely focus on relevance, retrieval, or compression, leaving this allocation trade-off implicit. We introduce MemPrice, which treats active context as a shared resource and dynamically allocates it across memories and representation levels. MemPrice turns accumulated memory pressure into an adaptive price on context, encouraging detail only when its estimated retention value justifies the additional footprint. This pressure persists across memory refreshes, allowing the contents of memory to evolve while preserving long-run control over context usage. We show that irreversible compression can force linear worst-case regret against hindsight following its own memory trajectory, and introduce a same-state benchmark to evaluate allocation on MemPrice's realized memory states. MemPrice enforces the hard context budget at every round and regulates long-run occupancy through adaptive pricing, without prior knowledge of the interaction horizon. Under priced-frontier regularity, its average allocation-regret bound against this benchmark vanishes when accumulated estimation error is sublinear. We evaluate the framework under matched memory budgets on LongMemEval, LoCoMo, AppWorld, and WebShop across three foundation models, spanning both query-blind memory construction and goal-directed agent context management.

title: Over-Defense in Coding Agents Begins at Silent Forks

payload.title: Over-Defense in Coding Agents Begins at Silent Forks
payload.abstract: Language models behind coding agents are post-trained with outcome rewards, and recent methods concentrate credit on the turns that decide the outcome. We find that defensive actions beyond what a task requires escape both. They begin at silent forks, the turns where every next action leads to the same outcome. Such actions leave the success rate unchanged, and frontier models take the disproportionate branch there in up to 91% of decisive actions under implicit budgets. The most direct fix, a checker in the trajectory reward, reaches these forks only through fully proportionate trajectories, leaving 74% of GRPO groups with identical rewards and behavior unchanged. This motivates a rethink of where learning signals belong, namely where behavior diverges, which a behavioral checker can locate and the outcome cannot. Our method, ForkDPO, contrasts a proportionate and a disproportionate action at the same prefix, at silent forks on both sides of the required behavior. On a test set of unseen repositories, it lowers a 4B model's disproportionate behavior from 70.3% to 58.9%, against 67.7% for DPO at randomly chosen turns, establishing behavioral divergence as a learning signal for how agents act beyond whether they finish. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Astarojth/silent-forks.

title: Robust Direct Preference Optimization under Preference Label-Flip Attacks

payload.title: Robust Direct Preference Optimization under Preference Label-Flip Attacks
payload.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is widely used for offline Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback. However, recent works have shown that DPO can be easily manipulated by adversarial preference label flip attacks, which are specifically designed to mislead the learner toward an attacker-chosen target policy. To address this issue, we design robust DPO methods that can defend against such attacks. Building on the property that lable flips induce parameter-independent gradient shifts in log-linear DPO, we propose Trim-$K$ Robust-DPO, which removes the $K$ highest-impact pairs, and Soft-Trim-$K$ Robust-DPO, which smoothly downweights them. We establish deterministic gradient perturbation bounds uniformly over all attack sets containing at most $K$ flips, explicitly separating defense-induced bias from surviving attack effects. Under bounded-region assumptions, these bounds yield time-uniform parameter and policy deviation guarantees. We further quantify how quadratic regularization improves curvature while introducing additional bias. Experiments on Stanford Human Preferences, HH-RLHF, and UltraFeedback-Binarized validate our analysis.

title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research

payload.title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research
payload.abstract: We present Épi, an autonomous research agent that sustains investigations across model sessions and evolves its methods through accumulated experience. Épi combines persistent research history, hierarchical memory, branching and independent review to maintain research continuity, learn from experiments, and explore and revisit alternative approaches. Its experiments run across session boundaries, and a fixed verifier evaluates their outputs. Épi produced 120 record-setting results, comprising 20 numerical bound records across 12 families and 100 construction records across eight families. These include an approximately 84-fold narrower interval for the $n$-queens constant and a more than 3.6-million-fold narrower rigorous interval for the quartic Feigenbaum attractor dimension. Exact dual certificates establish that the Cohn-Elkies linear-programming bound cannot be sharp in dimensions 10 and 11. Beyond numerical improvements, Épi gives a computer-assisted proof of Tuza's conjecture for split graphs with an eight-vertex clique part and at most three triangle-active neighborhood types, with arbitrary multiplicities. We extend this research process to algorithmic coding with Épi-turbo, a lightweight configuration that develops executable solvers for tasks including vehicle routing, scheduling and production planning. On 30 FrontierOR tasks, Épi-turbo achieves a 5.4% higher total benchmark score than Codex at 64% of its model cost, using the same underlying model and reasoning effort. Épi is designed to support human understanding by connecting computational results to explicit methods and mathematical arguments that researchers can examine and build upon.

title: LowNet: Looped Wavelet Neural Networks with 24 Learnable Parameters for Solving Poisson Equations

payload.title: LowNet: Looped Wavelet Neural Networks with 24 Learnable Parameters for Solving Poisson Equations
payload.abstract: Poisson equations frequently appear in various fields, such as mathematics, physics and informatics. Solving Poisson equation, however, is challenging. Traditional methods are not data-specific, although have high certainty. They require a large number of iterations due to the CFL numerical stability. In contrast, deep learning methods are data-driven and more efficient, but require accurate training data and suffer from heavy computation. To tackle these issues, we propose a wavelet-inspired Poisson solver with 24 trainable scalars. The proposed network has several advantages. First, it is compact. It has four independent $5\times5$ kernels, each represented by six parameters, leading to 24 scalars in total. Such compact format can be deployed on most devices. Second, thanks to the loop design, it achieves higher accuracy than previous methods. A residual loop reuses the wavelet block without increasing its parameters. Numerical experiments confirm that such loop indeed improves the solving accuracy. On 10000 images, one, two, and three loops of the wavelet block lead to PSNRs of $47.27$, $74.14$, and $100.74$ dB, respectively. Third, the proposed method is computationally fast. Thanks to the wavelet transform, the proposed method has linear computation complexity, leading to high computation performance. In short, we propose a novel looped wavelet neural network with compactness, accuracy and efficiency for solving Poisson equations. Our method can be applied in various fields, such as computational fluid dynamics, image reconstruction, biomedical engineering, electromagnetic field simulation.

title: T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training

payload.title: T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training
payload.abstract: Muon has recently emerged as a strong optimizer for large language model pretraining by exploiting matrix structure through polar orthogonalization. However, it processes each parameter matrix independently, whereas recent tensor-aware extensions of Muon jointly update groups of eligible matrix parameters through matrix unfoldings. In contrast, we propose T-MUON, a t-SVD-based generalization that groups structurally related Transformer gradients into third-order tensors and defines the corresponding Muon-style update directly through the $M$-transform. We show that the exact T-MUON update is a steepest-descent direction under the $\star_M$-spectral norm and establish a convergence guarantee. Across GPT-2-style and LLaMA-style models from 51M to 1.3B parameters trained on FineWeb and FineWeb-Edu, head-wise T-MUON with the identity transform consistently achieves lower validation perplexity than AdamW, Muon, and variants using DFT, DCT, or DST transforms. These gains persist in additional experiments with longer context lengths and larger token budgets, although the preferred tensorization mode varies across settings.

title: MLFont: Machine Learning-Driven Font Subsetting and Range-Compact Unicode-Range Slicing for Low-Latency Web Typography

payload.title: MLFont: Machine Learning-Driven Font Subsetting and Range-Compact Unicode-Range Slicing for Low-Latency Web Typography
payload.abstract: CSS3 @font-face rules with unicode-range descriptors partition web fonts into downloadable slices. While Latin fonts need ~20 KB in WOFF2, Pan-European (LGC) and East Asian (CJK) fonts contain 2,297-30,759 codepoints (158 KB-5.9 MB in WOFF2), where heuristic partitioning causes unused-glyph downloads, high HTTP RTT, CSS bloat, or missing-glyph fallbacks. We present MLFont, a machine learning and optimization framework that learns font slicing strategies from corpora via three stages: (1) a Zipfian High-Frequency Tier (most) isolating top-frequency codepoints; (2) a Latent Co-Occurrence Topic Tier using Online Variational Bayes LDA (Online LDA) or a Deep Neural Network Topic Model (DNNTM) with Shannon Entropy Difference Loss and Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization; and (3) a Memetic Range-Compact Genetic Algorithm (GA) with Potts-Viterbi dynamic programming and island bridging that minimizes topic discrepancy and CSS fragmentation. Across five Google Noto fonts (LGC, KR, JP, TC, SC), MLFont cuts 3G per-glyph latency by 56.7%-75.3% over single-file delivery and 46.1%-66.3% over equal-bin baselines on CJK with 100% coverage, reduces CSS intervals by 17.9%-41.7%, and achieves 1.56x-6.09x cold-cache speedups (65.4%-84.9% CJK and 44.7% LGC bandwidth savings) across 20 websites in simulator and Headless Chrome benchmarks (45/45 exact slice-set parity). Code: https://github.com/wq2012/mlfont Models: https://huggingface.co/collections/wq2012/mlfont

title: TrustAgent-RFF: Agentic Diagnostic Planning for Reliable RF Fingerprinting under Domain Shift

payload.title: TrustAgent-RFF: Agentic Diagnostic Planning for Reliable RF Fingerprinting under Domain Shift
payload.abstract: Radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) models can achieve accuracy under source domain conditions but become unreliable when the receiver, distance, collection day, or environment changes. Incorrect predictions in unseen domains may receive high softmax confidence, making confidence thresholding insufficient for trustworthy deployment. We propose TrustAgent-RFF, a prediction level reliability framework for RFF that operates with a frozen in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) classifier without target domain labels. For each device prediction, the framework acquires radio frequency evidence: counterfactual stability, prototype consistency, acquisition domain similarity, and signal quality. A source calibrated trust estimator combines these diagnostics with classifier confidence, prediction margin, and evidence availability indicators. Source derived lower tail penalties and cross module interactions reduce trust when diagnostic signals indicate weak support. A large language model (LLM) based planner adaptively selects the next diagnostic action based on evidence, trust state, action costs, and remaining budget. A deterministic source calibrated decision layer updates the prediction state as Accept, Reject, or Defer. Experiments across five RFF datasets and classifier backbones reveal an average source to target accuracy drop of 38.7% and show that many incorrect target domain predictions remain highly confident.

title: What Can't Jev Decide? Probing the Limits of One-Pass Decision Models

payload.title: What Can't Jev Decide? Probing the Limits of One-Pass Decision Models
payload.abstract: Jev and its open replicas choose among the options a caller supplies with a single forward pass, fast enough to decide inside an agent loop. We ask what such a model cannot decide, and find a simple limit: Jev cannot make a decision that an LLM makes only by writing out intermediate steps. On a benchmark that varies one factor at a time, Jev finds and selects records without error up to 20k tokens and 64 options, but once the answer depends on two or more updates of one user, accuracy falls, to 53-80% at sixteen updates, because similar records interfere. Given a stale summary of the state, Jev follows it. On real decision items graded by how many thinking tokens a reference LLM needs, Jev answers 97.5% of the items that one forward pass of that LLM solves, but only 74% of the others. Jev also does not know its limit: its confidence flags the errors it makes itself but not those it inherits from a stale input, and neither an explicit nor a trained hand-off option catches the latter. The open models we evaluate share these limits. Checking the state such models rely on requires a model that reasons.

title: Means-Ends Analysis Helps LLMs Plan in Continuous-State Domains

payload.title: Means-Ends Analysis Helps LLMs Plan in Continuous-State Domains
payload.abstract: LLM planning research has traditionally focused on discrete-state domains, where actions form a finite, enumerable set. Existing LLM planning frameworks largely assume actions are enumerable, modeling planning as a search process over candidate actions. However, in continuous-state domains, where actions form a continuum and cannot be enumerated, this assumption breaks down. We find a remedy in Newell and Simon's Means-Ends Analysis (MEA), a general problem-solving technique rooted in heuristics from human psychology. We develop Medaka, an MEA-inspired structured prompting framework that encourages recursive goal decomposition, algebraic derivation, and per-step state tracking. To evaluate native LLM planning abilities in continuous-state domains, we develop Liquidworld, a systematic testbed on liquid mixing. On Liquidworld, Medaka can improve performance across model families, suggesting that classical means-ends analysis elicits LLM-native reasoning abilities that are helpful for continuous-state planning.

title: Stable Signer V3: 4D Deformable Primitive Splatting Is All You Need for Sign Language Production

payload.title: Stable Signer V3: 4D Deformable Primitive Splatting Is All You Need for Sign Language Production
payload.abstract: We present Stable Signer V3, an interactive high-resolution sign language avatar system built on 4D Deformable Primitive Splatting. It addresses three limitations of existing avatars: restricted facial expression, inaccurate identity-specific body deformation, and loss of fine appearance details. Shared Face Primitive Splatting adds transferable superquadric primitives for richer expression control; Test-Time Body Primitive Splatting learns an identity-specific virtual muscle layer for more faithful motion; and Test-Time Tunneling Super-Resolution uses TunnelingNet to recover identity-specific high-resolution details. Both test-time modules are optimized once per signer identity; inference then runs entirely from the stored identity parameters. Together, they reduce facial geometry error by 71.4%, body-boundary error by 35.1% across ten identities, and high-resolution RGB reconstruction error by 24.2% on held-out evaluations, while retaining interactive streaming.

title: DF-PALM: Dynamic Fusion Prompt Learning for Audio--Language Models

payload.title: DF-PALM: Dynamic Fusion Prompt Learning for Audio--Language Models
payload.abstract: Few-shot audio classification requires audio--language models to distinguish variable acoustic events from limited labeled data. PALM's main formulation adapts encoded class representations without changing pretrained encoders, but its class representations remain input-independent and classification uses audio features without class-conditioned refinement. We introduce DF-PALM, a dynamic feature-space prompting framework that combines audio-conditioned class representations with asymmetric cross-attention for audio refinement.
