While prior works have identified decoding as a significant overhead and proposed pre-decoding filtering to mitigate it, we find that codec reference dependencies still force decoders to process many unselected frames, manifesting an over-decoding trap that bounds end-to-end throughput. This limitation stems from the reference-based design in modern codecs, which requires decoding preceding frames to reconstruct any selected one. As a result, over-decoding has become the practical bottleneck in VAPs using modern decoders, highlighting a critical but under-explored problem. To address this issue, we propose ParaDeco, a high-throughput video analytics framework featuring a novel frame-level parallel generative decoder. Unlike traditional decoders, ParaDeco adopts a decode-what-matters approach with decoupled frame dependencies. To decode arbitrary frames independently, ParaDeco generates frame-wise features as standalone skeletons using compressed video metadata, then predicts pseudo frames maintaining semantic consistency with original frames. Moreover, ParaDeco identifies which frames truly matter for analysis via delicate contribution-based frame filtering. We implement ParaDeco on a cloud server and evaluate it on large-scale real-world surveillance video datasets. Our experimental results show that ParaDeco achieves a 2.76× speedup on averagparse e compared to state-of-the-art VAPs.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Designing evaluation rubrics for the development of virtual human twins in healthcare.

payload.title: Designing evaluation rubrics for the development of virtual human twins in healthcare.
payload.abstract: Smart healthcare innovations driven by Virtual Human Twin (VHT) technology enable continuous patient monitoring. However, standards to assess their stage of development or a unified framework for performance comparisons are still lacking. This study aims to quantitatively analyze VHT-related studies, evaluate their development levels, and align them to the VHT roadmap. A systematic review guided by the PRISMA methodology was conducted, in which 26 studies representing different stages of VHT development were systematically analyzed. Articles were evaluated against an established 5-level roadmap and classified according to their closest alignment with black box, grey box, or surrogate VHTs. A rubric system was developed to assess VHT models to date, and their maturity was analyzed relative to the established roadmap. Among the 26 studies, all 5 roadmap levels were represented. Level 2 (Deductive stage) was the most frequently represented. Levels 4 and 5 (Evolutionary and Explainable stages) were represented only in 3 studies each. Among the included studies, VHT development appears fragmented, with significant hurdles in building VHTs with advanced functionality. The proposed rubric system may serve as an assessment tool to evaluate progress, encourage discussion, and improve experimental approaches for future VHTs, helping address challenges in advancing VHT development along the established roadmap.

title: Redefining 360° Video Navigation: A Novel Benchmark for Enhanced Immersive and Automated Exploration.

payload.title: Redefining 360° Video Navigation: A Novel Benchmark for Enhanced Immersive and Automated Exploration.
payload.abstract: 360° video navigation aims to model users' viewing behavior in immersive videos through continuous viewport selection. This task is challenging because human viewing is not driven by instantaneous responses to local saliency, but by continuous decisions that evolve with semantic events over time, involving attention shifts across events and long-term viewport changes. However, progress remains limited, mainly due to the lack of a well-established benchmark, resulting in limitations in data, annotation, and evaluation. Current datasets are limited in scale and diversity, and mostly consist of short or single-event videos, making cross-event viewing behavior underrepresented. Existing annotation methods rely on frame-level or short-term clustering, which emphasizes local consistency but fails to capture temporal continuity and the rationality of viewport selection during event transitions. Existing metrics focus on spatial overlap or trajectory consistency, ignoring motion-direction agreement between predicted and ground-truth navigation trajectories. As a result, spatially accurate predictions may still follow incorrect motion directions, leading to unreliable evaluation of viewing behavior. To address these issues, we construct a new benchmark for 360° video navigation in multi-event scenarios, with a standardized data and annotation pipeline and a more discriminative evaluation protocol. We further develop an event-level model to capture cross-event viewing behavior and long-term viewport evolution. Extensive experiments show that the proposed benchmark provides more reliable evaluation, and the proposed model achieves superior performance to existing methods.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: From data to personas: a multi-source approach to tailored online health information recommendation for ovarian cancer patients and caregivers.

payload.title: From data to personas: a multi-source approach to tailored online health information recommendation for ovarian cancer patients and caregivers.
payload.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OvCa) patients and caregivers face complex, evolving information needs, yet digital health platforms often lack tailoring. This study developed and validated computational personas to support a tailored recommender system (Health E-Librarian with Personalized Recommendations [HELPeR]) and address the cold-start problem, in which limited information about new users reduces the system's ability to generate relevant recommendations. We used a mixed-methods design integrating 4 data sources: (1) online OvCa forum posts (n = 457; 60 users), (2) semi-structured interviews with patients and caregivers (n = 20), (3) clinical case notes from a caregiver support program, and (4) expert input from gynecologic oncology nurses. Forum data were manually annotated and analyzed using k-modes clustering to identify user subgroups. Qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis, and findings were integrated to construct and refine personas. Five distinct user clusters were identified from forum data. Integration of multi-source data yielded 15 personas (9 patients, 6 caregivers) representing trajectories from diagnosis to end-of-life care. Patient personas captured needs related to symptom management, treatment decision-making, financial concerns, and psychosocial support, while caregiver personas emphasized communication, emotional burden, self-care, and care coordination. Personas reflected dynamic, context-dependent needs and were validated for clinical realism through expert review. Persona-based modeling provides an interpretable framework for tailored recommendation and approximates digital twin approaches, helping mitigate cold-start limitations. Multi-source persona development is a feasible strategy for enabling tailored digital health interventions and improving tailored information delivery in oncology care.

title: Self-MAR: Self-Supervised Multi-Stage Autoregressive Model for Water-Related Optical Image Enhancement.

payload.title: Self-MAR: Self-Supervised Multi-Stage Autoregressive Model for Water-Related Optical Image Enhancement.
payload.abstract: We propose Self-MAR, a self-supervised paradigm for water-related optical image enhancement that enables input-only restoration via the proposed VAR-inspired Multi-stage AutoRegressive model, in which each restoration stage is conditioned on the preceding restored state. The intricate interactions between light and the water medium introduce residual degradations that are difficult to model explicitly, thereby limiting the effectiveness of existing methods that rely heavily on synthetic data or sparse annotations. Furthermore, acquiring paired ground-truth data in real underwater environments remains challenging, giving rise to the triangular dilemma in underwater image enhancement (UIE). To address these issues, Self-MAR incorporates three key components: 1) We design a multi-stage, coarse-to-fine reconstruction architecture that progressively recovers image structure and suppresses content-coupled underwater object residuals (ORs) at different resolutions, transforming OR removal into structure-aware controllable image generation. 2) We construct an asymmetric phase-amplitude interaction that combines the structural phase of the current observation with the corrected spectral-energy distribution of the preceding restoration estimate. This interaction preserves spatial organization during stage-wise upsampling and propagates corrected color-energy statistics from coarse to fine. 3) We propose the Churning constraint mechanism to preserve the original perceptual features of the input image and prevent semantic drift during the self-supervised training process. Self-MAR derives supervision targets from the inputs themselves: underwater inputs generate OR-removal targets, while in-air inputs generate structural self-reconstruction targets from their own content.Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive full-reference restoration quality, leading performance across complementary no-reference metrics (UIQM, UCIQE, NIQE, and URANKER), efficient inference, and consistent performance across UIEB C60, UCCS, U45, and Z700. Downstream evaluation on SeaThru-D1 further shows the lowest combined depth-consistency error among thecompared state-of-the-art enhancement methods.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Current status and future outlook of artificial intelligence and automation in intravenous infusion systems.

payload.title: Current status and future outlook of artificial intelligence and automation in intravenous infusion systems.
payload.abstract: The combination of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and wearable biosensors is transforming healthcare by allowing continuous, real-time monitoring and more intelligent clinical decision-making. This review explores AI-driven monitoring, smart intravenous (IV) infusion automation, and wearable biosensors, and proposes Intelligent IV Automation and Smart Patient Synchronization (INFUSYNC), a conceptual framework synchronizing monitoring, automated fluid delivery, and predictive analytics. The literature shows meaningful progress: wearables increasingly support non-contact monitoring with near clinical-grade accuracy for select parameters, while infusion pumps with dose-error-reduction and AI-assisted decision support are reported to improve delivery precision and safety. Predictive models further support early detection of physiological decline. Progress remains uneven, however: most AI-enabled infusion systems are prototype-stage, closed-loop control remains rare, and interoperability, data security, and privacy remain underdeveloped. Future systems will need compatible, security-by-design, clinically validated, feedback-controlled architectures. Overall, this review outlines a clear but early-stage trajectory toward integrated smart-health environments for IV therapy.

title: From compliance to competence: a multi-level model for AI governance in undergraduate medical education.

payload.title: From compliance to competence: a multi-level model for AI governance in undergraduate medical education.
payload.abstract: AI's fast-paced irruption in medicine and education has challenged undergraduate medical colleges, with institutions documenting policies emphasizing immediate conduct restrictions, while strategic oversight, infrastructure and evaluation remain less consistently developed. We propose a multi-level framework for AI governance in undergraduate medical education based on accountability, competence and co-responsibility across institutions, educators and students, designed to turn a fast-evolving technology from a threat into an opportunity for collective progress.

title: DAAN: Mitigating Information Asymmetries for Point-Supervised Video Moment Retrieval.

payload.title: DAAN: Mitigating Information Asymmetries for Point-Supervised Video Moment Retrieval.
payload.abstract: Video Moment Retrieval (VMR), the task of identifying a specific moment in an untrimmed video from a natural language query, is a key capability for advanced video understanding. As an emerging research direction, point-supervised VMR offers a cost-effective solution by requiring minimal annotation efforts. In this paper, we explore the information asymmetries within this task: a semantic-positional asymmetry between the clarity of the visual cues and the imprecision of the annotated frame's position, and an instance-duration asymmetry between the certainty of a moment's occurrence and the ambiguity of its duration. To mitigate these asymmetries, we propose a novel framework, Dual-Asymmetry Aligned Network (DAAN), featuring two specialized components: (1) the Center-Guided Calibration module (CGC) which mitigates positional imprecision by dynamically generating a pseudo temporal center and leveraging a decomposed cross-modal attention strategy to recalibrate the feature distribution to align semantic attention with the estimated event centroid; and (2) the Duration-Aware Proposal Discriminator (DPD) which alleviates duration ambiguity by distinguishing the most plausible temporal spans. It infers missing duration information by learning query-conditioned structural compatibility between proposal content and boundary representations. Extensive experiments on TACoS, ActivityNet Captions, and Charades-STA validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework in point-supervised VMR.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Camera-Incremental Person Re-Identification Via Geometric Representation Evolution.

payload.title: Camera-Incremental Person Re-Identification Via Geometric Representation Evolution.
payload.abstract: Person re-identification (ReID) is a core technology in large-scale intelligent surveillance systems. In practical deployments, surveillance networks evolve continuously as new cameras are incrementally integrated. As the network expands, the system not only encounters new identities but also captures previously known identities from novel camera views. However, existing LReID studies typically assume disjoint identity spaces across stages, failing to model the cumulative evolution of features induced by such expansion. To bridge this gap, we introduce Camera-Incremental Person Re-Identification (CIReID), a challenging setting that requires continuously updating representations from newly added cameras without access to historical raw data. Unlike traditional closed-set forgetting, the primary challenge in CI-ReID lies in feature space distortion and representation fragmentation across domain shifts. To address this, we propose Camera-Incremental Geometric Representation Evolution (CIGRE). First, we introduce a Dynamic Geometric Alignment (DGA) mechanism, which flexibly expands an Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF) classifier to provide a stable and scalable discriminative geometric skeleton for the evergrowing identity set. Building upon this stable structure, we propose a Cross-Camera Identity Consolidation (CCIC) strategy. By maintaining momentum-updated global prototypes, CCIC progressively aggregates the fragmented identity features revealed under novel views. Furthermore, we establish a new CI-ReID benchmark derived from standard datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CIGRE effectively scales with longterm camera expansion and achieves state-of-the-art performance by strictly maintaining cross-camera consistency. Our code and models will be released.

title: From authoring to editing: a competency framework for trainee use of ambient AI clinical documentation.

payload.title: From authoring to editing: a competency framework for trainee use of ambient AI clinical documentation.
payload.abstract: Ambient AI has spread through clinical settings faster than curricula can adapt, shifting trainee documentation from authoring to editing notes. Authoring historically honed clinical reasoning for trainees, yet medical education is not prepared to develop the editing task now replacing it. We define this task as a teachable competency with four domains - error detection, clinical reconciliation, independent generation, and trust calibration - and describe how simulation can teach them.

title: HyHO-DDI: A hypergraph neural network for high-order Drug-Drug interaction prediction.

payload.title: HyHO-DDI: A hypergraph neural network for high-order Drug-Drug interaction prediction.
payload.abstract: Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) are a major cause of adverse drug reactions (ADRs), particularly in patients receiving multiple medications. Existing computational methods predominantly focus on pairwise interactions, limiting their ability to capture the complex effects of high-order (multi-drug) therapies. This study proposes a computational framework for predicting myopathy-associated high-order DDIs. We propose HyHO-DDIs, a hypergraph neural network model for predicting myopathy-associated high-order drug combinations using a dataset curated from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). In our model, each drug is represented by molecular fingerprint features and a protein-target profile, and we construct a hypergraph in which nodes are drugs and hyperedges correspond to multi-drug combinations co-reported with myopathy. The model integrates Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) layers with hypergraph-based attention to learn high-order interaction representations, and a decoder outputs the predicted probability of a myopathy association for an input drug combination. We evaluated HyHO-DDI with 5-fold cross-validation and compared it against an MLP with the same inputs, as well as established high-order baselines (HODDI, D3I), and DeepPSE on the pairwise subset. HyHO-DDI achieved strong overall performance across combination sizes and remained competitive with DeepPSE on the pairwise subset, achieving the same F1-score with higher recall. For larger combinations, the proposed model reduced false-positive predictions while maintaining strong performance on previously unseen drug combinations, demonstrating robust generalization. HyHO-DDI provides an effective framework for predicting myopathy-associated high-order DDIs by explicitly modeling multi-drug interactions with hypergraphs. The proposed approach has the potential to improve computational pharmacovigilance by prioritizing potentially hazardous drug combinations and supporting medication safety.

title: Six pragmatic steps to separate medical GenAI's promise from its inherent dangers.

payload.title: Six pragmatic steps to separate medical GenAI's promise from its inherent dangers.
payload.abstract: GenAI and agentic systems in medicine bring real opportunities for better diagnosis and therapy and for the development of better diagnoses and therapies. It is now increasingly being recognised that the power of these systems for good is inseparable from their power to be used for harm. Systems optimised for biomedical research are unfortunately being harnessed by malign human masters to help develop bioweapons to be targeted at humanity. Agentic systems are autonomously, unknown to their human masters, carrying out cybersecurity attacks. Frontier models are increasing anxiety and stress of medical students and threaten to reshape medical professional roles, not always for the better. Although  there may currently be some over emphasis of risk by BigTech foundation model developers, and these may even be attempts at ‘regulatory capture’, there are also genuine reasons for concern. We set out actionable measures that are needed to control medical frontier models to maximise human benefits and control risks.

title: A harmonized SNOMED Clinical Terms components quality assurance framework.

payload.title: A harmonized SNOMED Clinical Terms components quality assurance framework.
payload.abstract: The objective of this study was to construct a harmonized SNOMED Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) components quality assurance framework for identifying, categorizing, and assessing data quality issues in SNOMED CT components. We constructed the framework through an iterative process that analyzed SNOMED CT's core components, synthesized quality factors from prior literature, reviewed inactivation reasons, and SNOMED CT release validation framework, and refined error categories through a targeted review of SNOMED CT error studies. The framework was tested using a case study evaluation. The resulting harmonized SNOMED CT components quality assurance framework consists of 2 dimensions: (1) SNOMED CT core components (concept, description, subtype relationships, attribute relationships) and (2) quality factors (clarity, conciseness, consistency, correctness, comprehensive domain coverage, currency, completeness, conformance). The quality factors were also defined by error categories (omission, commission). The framework integrates previously reported quality factors, SNOMED CT inactivation reasons, release validation methods, and includes component-specific error definitions to standardize how quality issues are categorized and assessed. It extends prior frameworks, supports consistent terminology governance, enables measurable quality indicators, and provides a structured foundation for auditing methods and comparative evaluation across SNOMED CT versions and releases. The harmonized framework provides a common vocabulary and structure for describing and classifying quality issues in SNOMED CT. It can guide the development and comparison of auditing methods, support terminology governance, and inform quality-improvement activities undertaken by SNOMED International and national release centers.

title: Deep Time-Series Forecasting in 10 Years: A Survey.

payload.title: Deep Time-Series Forecasting in 10 Years: A Survey.
payload.abstract: Autocorrelation is a common property of time-series, where each observation is dependent on its predecessors. In deep time-series forecasting, it raises two central challenges: ❶ designing backbone architectures to model autocorrelation in history sequences, and ❷ devising loss functions to model autocorrelation in label sequences. Recent studies have made strides in tackling these challenges, but a systematic survey examining both aspects remains lacking. To bridge this gap, this paper reviews deep time-series forecasting from an autocorrelation modeling perspective, offering two contributions beyond existing surveys. First, it introduces a taxonomy that jointly covers both backbone architectures and loss functions, whereas prior surveys provide limited coverage of the latter. Second, it analyzes the motivations and insights underlying the surveyed literature from a unified autocorrelation modeling perspective, providing a holistic overview of the field's evolution.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Learning Video Exposure Correction: Large-Scale Real-World Dataset and Method.

payload.title: Learning Video Exposure Correction: Large-Scale Real-World Dataset and Method.
payload.abstract: Exposure correction aims to enhance visual data degraded by improper exposures, thereby improving perceptual quality. While substantial progress has been achieved in single-image exposure correction, its extension to videos remains largely underexplored. Applying frame- wise correction methods to videos often results in flickering artifacts and degraded visual coherence. Progress in video exposure correction has also been hindered by the lack of a large-scale paired benchmark. To address this limitation, we introduce a real-world paired video exposure correction dataset that covers both underexposed and overexposed dynamic scenes. The dataset comprises 36 K spatially aligned frame pairs acquired using a dual-camera acquisition system equipped with a beam splitter, which enables synchronized recording of ill-exposed and well-exposed videos. Based on this dataset, we develop an end-to-end dual-stream Retinex framework that jointly handles underexposure and overexposure through exposure-aware temporal modeling. To mitigate exposure-induced interference during temporal alignment, our framework aggregates the amplitude spectra of neighboring frames into a shared exposure representation while retaining phase-derived structural information for cross-frame correspondence. The framework further reinterprets residual inter-frame discrepancies as pseudo- gradient cues for inverted attention, enabling temporal fusion to preserve complementary information while suppressing unreliable content. Finally, a learned restoration module combines the disentangled reflectance and dual-stream illumination components to produce temporally consistent exposure-corrected frames. The extensive experiments based on various evaluations and user studies demonstrate the significance of our dataset and the effectiveness of our method. Our dataset is available at https://dx.doi.org/10.21227/w9yn-y292.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: XS-VID: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Small Object Detection and Tracking in Videos.

payload.title: XS-VID: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Small Object Detection and Tracking in Videos.
payload.abstract: Small object detection and tracking in videos remain critical yet underexplored challenges in computer vision, particularly for applications such as public safety, aerial surveillance, and autonomous driving. Existing benchmarks offer limited support due to limited numbers of small objects, constrained category diversity, and narrow scene coverage. To address these limitations, we introduce XS-VID, a large-scale video benchmark comprising 223K frames and 1.4M annotated bounding boxes across 374 video sequences spanning diverse scene types. XS-VID provides extensive coverage of small-object scales, particularly for extremely small (0 ∼ 122 pixels) and small (122 ∼ 20 2  pixels) objects, which collectively constitute over 55% of all annotations. For systematic evaluation, we establish three dedicated tracks: Detection, multiple object tracking (MOT), and single object tracking (SOT), and extensively test the existing state-of-the-art methods on each. The experimental results indicate that existing methods face significant challenges with XS-VID, mainly stemming from insufficient modeling of spatiotemporal features at small scales. To tackle these challenges, we propose a lightweight, high-precision detection framework dubbed YOLOFT. It enhances small-object feature representation and spatiotemporal integration while preserving high detection speed,thereby achieving improved accuracy and robustness onboth the XS-VID and VisDrone benchmarks.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: MaskGaussian++: Probabilistic Masks for General 3D Gaussian Representation.

payload.title: MaskGaussian++: Probabilistic Masks for General 3D Gaussian Representation.
payload.abstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has demonstrated remarkable performance in novel view synthesis and realtime rendering, the high memory consumption due to the use of millions of Gaussians limits its practicality. To mitigate this issue, improvements have been made by pruning unnecessary Gaussians, either through a hand-crafted criterion or by using learned masks. However, these methods deterministically remove Gaussians based on a snapshot of the pruning moment, leading to sub-optimized reconstruction performance from a long-term perspective. To address this issue, we introduce MaskGaussian++, which models Gaussians as probabilistic entities rather than permanently removing them, and utilize them according to their probability of existence. To achieve this, we propose a masked-rasterization technique that enables unused yet probabilistically existing Gaussians to receive gradients, allowing for dynamic assessment of their contribution to the evolving scene and adjustment of their probability of existence. Beyond vanilla 3DGS, this probabilistic masking is a model-agnostic mechanism for the broader Gaussian family: we adapt it to neural (anchor-based) Gaussians with a shared anchor mask, and to distributed multi- GPU Gaussians with a distributed masked-rasterizer, through which we further uncover a log-linear scaling law of Gaussian Splatting spanning up to 90 million primitives, and to dynamic 4D Gaussians with a single time-invariant per-primitive mask that transfers across two structurally different 4D representations. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method: on vanilla 3DGS it prunes over 60% of Gaussians on average with only a 0.02 PSNR decline, halves the storage of neural Gaussians, scales $2\times$ more efficiently than Grendel-GS in large-scale distributed training, and compressing dynamic 4D Gaussians several-fold at on-par or better quality.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: MotionRFT: Unified Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Text-to-Motion Generation.

payload.title: MotionRFT: Unified Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Text-to-Motion Generation.
payload.abstract: Text-to-motion generation has advanced with diffusion- and flow-based generative models, yet supervised pre-training remains insufficient to align models with high-level objectives such as semantic consistency, realism, and human preference. Existing post-training methods have key limitations: they (1) target a specific motion representation, such as joints, (2) optimize a particular aspect, such as text-motion alignment, and may compromise other factors; and (3) incur substantial computational overhead, data dependence, and coarse-grained optimization. We present a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that comprises a heterogeneous-representation, multi-dimensional reward model, MotionReward, and an efficient, fine-grained fine-tuning method, EasyTune. To obtain a unified semantics representation, MotionReward maps heterogeneous motions into a shared semantic space anchored by text, enabling multi-dimensional reward learning; Self-refinement Preference Learning further enhances semantics without additional annotations. For efficient and effective fine-tuning, we identify the recursive gradient dependence across denoising steps as the key bottleneck, and propose EasyTune, which optimizes step-wise rather than over the full trajectory, yielding dense, fine-grained, and memory-efficient updates. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our framework, achieving FID 0.132 at 22.10 GB peak memory for MLD model and saving up to 15.22 GB over DRaFT. It reduces FID by 22.9% on joint-based ACMDM, and achieves a 12.1% R-Precision gain and 21.7% FID improvement on rotation-based HY-Motion.

title: A Survey on Archetypal Analysis.

payload.title: A Survey on Archetypal Analysis.
payload.abstract: Archetypal analysis (AA) was originally proposed in 1994 by Adele Cutler and Leo Breiman as a computational procedure for extracting distinct aspects, so-called archetypes, from observations, with each observational record approximated as a mixture (i.e., convex combination) of these archetypes. AA thereby provides straightforward, interpretable, and explainable representations for feature extraction and dimensionality reduction, facilitating the understanding of the structure of high-dimensional data and enabling wide applications across the sciences. However, AA also faces challenges, particularly as the associated optimization problem is nonconvex. This is the first survey that provides researchers and data mining practitioners with an overview of the methodologies and opportunities that AA offers, surveying the many applications of AA across disparate fields of science, as well as best practices for modeling data with AA and its limitations. The survey concludes by explaining crucial future research directions concerning AA.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Reverberation: Learning the Latencies Before Forecasting Trajectories.

payload.title: Reverberation: Learning the Latencies Before Forecasting Trajectories.
payload.abstract: Bridging the past to the future, connecting agents both spatially and temporally, lies at the core of the trajectory prediction task. Despite great efforts, it remains challenging to explicitly learn and predict latencies, i.e., response intervals or temporal delays with which agents respond to various trajectory changing events and adjust their future paths, whether on their own or interactively. Different agents may exhibit distinct latency preferences for noticing, processing, and reacting to a specific trajectory-changing event. The lack of consideration of such latencies may undermine the temporal continuity of forecasting systems, leading to implausible or unintended trajectories. Inspired by reverberation in acoustics, we propose a new reverberation transform and the corresponding Reverberation (Rev for short) trajectory prediction model, which predicts both individual latency preferences and their stochastic variations accordingly, by using two explicit and learnable reverberation kernels, enabling latency-conditioned and controllable trajectory prediction under both non-interactive and social latencies. Experiments on multiple datasets, whether of pedestrians or vehicles, demonstrate that Rev achieves competitive accuracy while revealing interpretable latency dynamics across agents and scenarios. Qualitative analyses further verify the properties of the reverberation transform, highlighting its potential as a general latency modeling approach.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Causal Effect Estimation Under Networked Interference Without Networked Unconfoundedness Assumption.

payload.title: Causal Effect Estimation Under Networked Interference Without Networked Unconfoundedness Assumption.
payload.abstract: Estimating causal effects under networked interference from observational data is a crucial yet challenging problem. Most existing methods mainly rely on the networked unconfoundedness assumption, which guarantees the identification of networked effects. However, this assumption is often violated due to the latent confounders inherent in observational data, thereby hindering the identification of networked effects. To address this issue, we leverage the rich interaction patterns between units in networks, which provide valuable information for recovering these latent confounders. Building on this insight, we develop a confounder recovery framework that explicitly characterizes three categories of latent confounders in networked settings: those affecting only the unit, those affecting only the unit's neighbors, and those influencing both. Based on this framework, we design a networked effect estimator using identifiable representation learning techniques. From a theoretical standpoint, we prove the identifiability of all three types of latent confounders and, by leveraging the recovered confounders, establish a formal identification result for networked effects. Extensive experiments validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Discovering Visual Co-occurrence for Fine-grained Image Retrieval.

payload.title: Discovering Visual Co-occurrence for Fine-grained Image Retrieval.
payload.abstract: Recent fine-grained image retrieval work predominantly focuses on learning diverse visual patterns from training set and further improving the generalization capability when confronted with unseen categories. However, such a design under-exploits the compositional structure of fine-grained objects, leading to rare semantics being easily overwhelmed by more universal ones, such as large-range bird feathers, and even overlooked. Consequently, it fails to identify unknown subcategories characterized by these rare semantics, thereby decreasing retrieval performance. As a remedy, we propose a novel Visual Co-occurrence Discovery Network (VCDN) to discover semantic co-occurring relationships within objects and facilitate the inference of their compositional structures. VCDN leverages the object's compositional structures to ensure equal representation of diverse semantics, reducing the dominance of more universal semantics and highlighting rare ones. Technically, VCDN involves initially employing a sliding-window sampling strategy to uniformly extract local regions from images. From these regions, visual semantics are distilled to identify comprehensive visual representation within objects. Recognizing the disparity in saliency within these semantics, VCDN establishes local intra-semantic correspondences to adjust their saliency levels, leveraging complementary information from semantically related concepts. Furthermore, co-occurring relationships among diverse semantics are dynamically modeled through grouping and interaction, enabling precise inference of the object's compositional structure and emphasizing rare semantics. Quantitative and qualitative experiments show that VCDN achieves promising performance on fine-grained and product retrieval datasets.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: A Depth Complementary Framework for Monocular 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Driving.

payload.title: A Depth Complementary Framework for Monocular 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Driving.
payload.abstract: Monocular 3D object detection offers a cost-effective solution for 3D localization from a single image in autonomous driving, yet its accuracy remains fundamentally limited by depth estimation due to the ill-posed nature of 2D-to-3D mapping. Existing methods attempt to reduce estimation variance by ensembling predictions from multiple depth branches that primarily rely on local cues. However, we observe that these estimates exhibit systematic one-sided biases, where depth prediction errors for the same object tend to be predominantly either positive or negative. To address this limitation, we propose MonoCD, a novel framework that enhances depth complementarity through two key innovations. First, we introduce a depth branch that incorporates ground elevation as a global cue to complement conventional local cues. Second, we develop a bias-compensating formulation for depth prediction that applies an opposite-signed design to local cues, actively counteracting their systematic biases. Owing to these two components, MonoCD achieves substantially improved depth complementarity by generating more anti-correlated estimates. Extensive experiments on the KITTI and Waymo benchmarks show that MonoCD achieves state-of-the-art performance. Moreover, the proposed depth branch is lightweight and plug-and-play, making it readily applicable to boost existing monocular 3D detection frameworks.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Five safes task execution service: a standards-based architecture and reference implementation for secure federated analytics across trusted research environments.

payload.title: Five safes task execution service: a standards-based architecture and reference implementation for secure federated analytics across trusted research environments.
payload.abstract: Design, implement, and evaluate a standards-based architecture for secure federated analytics across heterogeneous Trusted Research Environments (TREs) that aligns with the Five Safes Framework, without requiring TREs to modify their internal governance, infrastructure, or operational practices. The Five Safes task execution service (TES) architecture standardizes the format of analysis requests and handles analysis execution and release of outputs consistent with the Five Safes Framework. The Global Alliance for Genomics and Health TES standard is used for submitting analyses to TREs. Three logical layers support federated analytics: a Submission and Orchestration Layer outside the TRE accepts analyses and holds outputs for collection; a Controller Layer inside the TRE enforces local governance policies and manages disclosure control; and an Analysis Execution Layer governs the technical execution of approved analytics against sensitive data. An open-source reference implementation was developed and deployed in 2 real-world case studies. Five Safes TES was deployed to enable federated analytics within the Dementias Platform UK national research infrastructure. In a transcontinental deployment, federated analytics across 2 TREs hosted in Singapore was enabled by Submission and Orchestration Layers hosted in the United Kingdom, demonstrating multi-jurisdictional federated analytics without centralizing control or moving sensitive data. By aligning open technical standards with established governance frameworks, the architecture supports heterogeneous TREs participating in federated analyses while preserving data sovereignty, institutional autonomy, and compliance with local governance requirements. Five Safes TES demonstrates how TRE federated analytics can be deployed as a routine research capability, rather than requiring bespoke technical development.

title: Health information technology deregulation jeopardizes patient safety and public health.

payload.title: Health information technology deregulation jeopardizes patient safety and public health.
payload.abstract: In this Perspective, we provide the rationale for the retention of safety-critical certification criteria for health information technology by the Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC). To not do so puts all future American patients at risk. The proposed deregulatory actions are based on faulty premises, will lead to serious adverse patient outcomes, and sets a dangerous precedent. Public safety regulations should be held to a higher standard than other regulations, as a central role of government is to protect the general population from the actions of individuals and entities who may have incentives to create potentially harmful products or services.

title: Learning Group Interactions and Semantic Intentions for Multi-Object Trajectory Prediction.

payload.title: Learning Group Interactions and Semantic Intentions for Multi-Object Trajectory Prediction.
payload.abstract: Effective modeling of group interactions and dynamic semantic intentions is crucial for forecasting behaviors like trajectories or movements. In complex scenarios like sports, agents' trajectories are influenced by group interactions and intentions, including team strategies and opponent actions. To this end, we propose a novel diffusion-based trajectory prediction framework that integrates group-level interactions into a conditional diffusion model, enabling the generation of diverse trajectories aligned with specific group activity. To capture dynamic semantic intentions, we frame group interaction prediction as a cooperative game, using Banzhaf interaction to model cooperation trends. We then fuse semantic intentions with enhanced agent embeddings, which are refined through both global and local aggregation. Furthermore, we expand the NBA SportVU dataset by adding human annotations of team-level tactics for trajectory and tactic prediction tasks. Extensive experiments on three widely adopted datasets demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

title: Rethinking the Aggregation Head: Competitive Slot Distillation for Robust Visual Place Recognition.

payload.title: Rethinking the Aggregation Head: Competitive Slot Distillation for Robust Visual Place Recognition.
payload.abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) localizes a query image by retrieving the best-matching place from a large-scale geo-tagged database. Its key challenge lies in aggregating the stable structural cues from distractor-saturated scenes into a global descriptor. Existing aggregation methods follow a single-pass paradigm that struggles to fully disentangle informative cues from distractors, and largely offload this unresolved burden onto auxiliary external modules. Inspired by natural selection, we recast aggregation as an iterative structure-distillation process, in which stable structural cues are progressively reinforced through competition, while distractor responses are suppressed to guide later iterations toward more reliable regions. Specifically, we propose the Competitive Slot Distillation (CoSDi) framework, which uses only 20 dynamically updatable learnable prototypes ($i.e.$, slots) that interact with scene features to form an affinity matrix, and imposes a zero-sum assignment along the slot dimension to drive the slots to specialize in complementary structures. Since the competition itself reveals which regions are most strongly absorbed by the slots, this affinity matrix can be directly reused as an intrinsic filtering signal to suppress unreliable regions without any auxiliary model ($e.g.$, segmentation), allowing subsequent competition to refocus on a cleaner feature pool and forming a self-reinforcing competition-filtering-refocusing loop. Experiments on eight VPR benchmarks show that CoSDi outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with a $+4.3\%$ R@1 increase on Nordland, a structurally sparse dataset with drastic seasonal changes. Moreover, without task-specific modification, CoSDi transfers directly to Cross-View Geo-Localization (CVGL), achieving a $+6.09\%$ R@1 gain over MEAN on SUES-200 Drone $\to$ Satellite cross-dataset generalization, demonstrating transferability beyond its original street-level VPR setting.
payload.journal: IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell

title: Delving Deep Into Unraveling Spatio-Temporal Forgery Cues for Face Forgery Video Detection.

payload.title: Delving Deep Into Unraveling Spatio-Temporal Forgery Cues for Face Forgery Video Detection.
payload.abstract: Face Forgery Video Detection is a critical yet challenging task in determining whether a digital facial video is authentic or forged. Existing methods often rely on isolated spatial or coarsely fused spatio-temporal features, which are insufficient to mine spatio-temporal forgery cues and lead to unsatisfactory generalization performance. To this end, we strive to unravel general spatio-temporal forgery cues across three progressive levels: (1) spatial regional suspicions, (2) temporal momentary anomalies and gradual inconsistencies, and (3) spatio-temporal cumulative distortions. Accordingly, we design a hierarchical cooperation module to identify regional suspicion cues by coordinating intra-frame features across different Transformer layers of Image Encoder. Then, we devise a gradual future guidance module to unravel temporal cues by iteratively aggregating historical anomaly cues and gradually propagating inconsistency cues into future frames. Finally, we introduce a historical review module that unravels distortion cues via momentum accumulation and spatio-temporal review from future to historical frames. These three modules form Spatio-Temporal Forgery Cue Unraveling (STFCU) framework, sequentially highlighting spatial discriminative features by unraveling spatio-temporal forgery cues bidirectionally between historical and future frames. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate effectiveness of STFCU method, achieving state-of-the-art performance across diverse unseen datasets and manipulation methods.

title: Association of medical discrimination and hypertension in adults in the All of Us Research Program.

payload.title: Association of medical discrimination and hypertension in adults in the All of Us Research Program.
payload.abstract: To examine the associations of medical discrimination with hypertension (HTN) outcomes. Using cross-sectional data from the All of Us Research Program (2018-2022), we defined elevated blood pressure (BP) as systolic BP ≥130 or diastolic BP ≥ 80 mm Hg. We defined HTN diagnosis as either (1) self-reported HTN or (2) a HTN billing code. Among participants with HTN, we assessed antihypertensive medication use and HTN control. Logistic regression models estimated the associations of medical discrimination (using the Discrimination in Medical Settings Scale) with each BP outcome. The full sample included 29 805 adults, of whom 10 359 adults had elevated BP. Medical discrimination was associated with higher odds of elevated BP (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 1.05, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02-1.08) and HTN diagnosis (AOR 1.06, 95% CI, 1.02-1.10). Among participants with HTN, medical discrimination was not associated with treatment or control. Findings suggest that medical discrimination contributes to increased prevalence of elevated BP and HTN diagnosis. Researchers should examine mechanisms linking medical discrimination with HTN.

title: An Evaluation of Practitioner Competency and Practices in Diagnosing and Managing Keratoconus in Malawi: A Cross-Sectional Analysis

payload.title: An Evaluation of Practitioner Competency and Practices in Diagnosing and Managing Keratoconus in Malawi: A Cross-Sectional Analysis
payload.abstract: This study assessed eye care practitioners’ competencies, clinical practices, and barriers related to KC diagnosis and management in Malawi. A national cross-sectional study was conducted among eye care practitioners in Malawi. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing demographics, self-reported competency in KC diagnosis and management, clinical practices, service availability, and barriers to care. Data analysis was conducted using Stata version 15 and R version 4.5.1. A total of 110 practitioners participated (response rate: 58.5%). The mean age was 35.4 ± 7.4 years, and optometrists constituted 60.9% of respondents. Diagnostic competency scores were consistently higher than management competency scores across knowledge, skills, and experience domains. Higher educational attainment was independently associated with diagnostic competency, with undergraduate (aOR = 3.3; 95% CI: 1.13–9.63) and postgraduate practitioners (aOR = 6.6; 95% CI: 1.91–22.62) demonstrating greater odds of competency than diploma holders. Equipment shortages were significantly associated with facility type (p = 0.035), while other barriers showed no significant variation across regions or levels of care. Eye care practitioners in Malawi reported moderate competency in KC diagnosis and management, with stronger confidence in diagnosis than management. Strengthening practitioner training, improving access to diagnostic technologies, and enhancing affordability of contact lens services may improve KC care delivery and visual outcomes.

title: Outcomes of Intravitreal Anti-VEGF Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Kazakhstan

payload.title: Outcomes of Intravitreal Anti-VEGF Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Kazakhstan
payload.abstract: Background: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss among older adults. Although randomised controlled trials have demonstrated the robust efficacy of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, real-world outcomes often differ markedly from trial findings. This study aimed to evaluate the anatomical and functional outcomes of anti-VEGF therapy in a clinical cohort of nAMD patients, including a subgroup that received adjunctive rescue photodynamic therapy (PDT) with verteporfin. Methods: This single-centre, retrospective observational cohort study included 568 patients (634 eyes) with nAMD treated with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections. Bevacizumab was used in 49% of eyes, ranibizumab in 44%, and aflibercept in 7%. Best recorded visual acuity (BRVA) and central retinal thickness (CRT) measured by optical coherence tomography (OCT) were recorded at baseline and at the final documented follow-up. Eyes with eccentric fixation were excluded from BRVA analysis but were retained for CRT analysis. Results: Mean patient age was 71.7 ± 8.8 years, and 67.6% of eyes were from female patients. The mean number of anti-VEGF injections was 5 ± 5.3 per eye; the mean follow-up duration was 11.5 months. Mean CRT decreased significantly from 347.3 ± 27.5 μm at baseline to 324.9 ± 28.8 μm at final follow-up (p < 0.001). Mean BRVA (logMAR) improved modestly from 0.98 ± 0.55 (Snellen ~20/190; ~35 ETDRS letters) to 0.93 ± 0.56 (Snellen ~20/175; ~37.5 ETDRS letters) (p < 0.001), with 67.9% of eyes demonstrating BRVA stability (change < 0.1 logMAR). Rescue PDT was administered in 10.3% of eyes. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort, anti-VEGF therapy was associated with significant anatomical improvement, as measured by CRT reduction, while functional outcomes were characterised by visual stabilisation rather than substantial gains.

title: Macular Pigment Optical Density Is Not Associated with Contrast Sensitivity When Measured with 520 nm Monochromatic Stimuli

payload.title: Macular Pigment Optical Density Is Not Associated with Contrast Sensitivity When Measured with 520 nm Monochromatic Stimuli
payload.abstract: Macular pigments (MP; lutein, zeaxanthin, and meso-zeaxanthin) filter short-wavelength light and have been linked to reduced glare and enhanced visual performance. Whether macular pigment optical density (MPOD) is associated with contrast sensitivity (CS) under conditions of minimal MP absorption remains unclear. Fifty-two adults (mean age = 23.5 ± 8.0 years; range = 18–58 years; 85% < 25 years) participated. MPOD was measured using customized heterochromatic flicker photometry. CS was assessed monocularly in the same eye at five spatial frequencies (1.6, 3.2, 8, 16, and 24 cycles/degree), using a custom optical system with narrowband 520 nm laser stimuli. No significant correlations were found between MPOD and CS at any spatial frequency (all |r| ≤ 0.08, all p ≥ 0.59), including when individual area estimates were made for each participant’s curve (area under the logged CSF). Separate partial correlations controlling for iris lightness or habitual visual correction were also non-significant. Although MP has been shown to be related to CS when measured under glare or blue haze conditions, these findings suggest that when filtering by MP is minimized, direct effects on CS, especially on the young healthy eye, are likely minimal.

title: Individual Differences in Perceived Complexity, Visual Discomfort, and Preference for Images Varying in Spectral Scaling

payload.title: Individual Differences in Perceived Complexity, Visual Discomfort, and Preference for Images Varying in Spectral Scaling
payload.abstract: Participants (N = 89) rated preference, discomfort, and perceived complexity of grayscale, thresholded, edge and mountain profile images varying in spectral scaling properties. Participants also completed self-report questionnaires designed to measure neurodivergent (CATI, ASRS) or sensory processing sensitivity (CHYPS-V, SPQ-S). Across image types, perceived complexity and discomfort declined as the spectral slope parameter increased, whereas preference increased from the shallowest to the intermediate slopes and then plateaued. Self-reported autistic-like traits, ADHD-like traits, and sensory sensitivity were largely unrelated to overall rating levels but showed small associations with how ratings changed across spectral slope. These findings support treating complexity, discomfort, and preference as related but non-equivalent visual judgments, with trait-related influences expressed mainly as modest variation in sensitivity to spectral scaling.

title: Retinitis Pigmentosa: A Review of Its Pathogenesis and Emerging Molecular and Cellular Therapies

payload.title: Retinitis Pigmentosa: A Review of Its Pathogenesis and Emerging Molecular and Cellular Therapies
payload.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is the most common inherited retinal dystrophy and remains largely untreatable. This review summarizes RP pathogenesis and critically appraises emerging therapeutic strategies, including gene augmentation, gene editing, RNA-based therapies, gene-agnostic and neuroprotective approaches, stem-cell therapy and their delivery platforms. We compare these strategies according to mutation mechanism, disease stage, durability, delivery route, and current level of clinical evidence. Although several approaches have shown improved structural and functional outcomes in preclinical and early-phase studies, RPE65-directed gene augmentation (voretigen neparvovec) remains the only approved therapy, and even it does not halt degeneration. For most modalities, long-term efficacy, safety, durability and clinical validation are not yet established, and translation is further constrained by delivery, immunogenicity, manufacturing, and cost. Rather than a realized paradigm shift, current evidence points to a rapidly advancing but still largely investigational field with successful clinical translation remaining elusive.

title: Assessment of the Efficacy and Safety of CyberKnife Radiosurgery on Optic Nerve Sheath Meningiomas

payload.title: Assessment of the Efficacy and Safety of CyberKnife Radiosurgery on Optic Nerve Sheath Meningiomas
payload.abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CyberKnife (CK) radiosurgery in patients with optic nerve sheath meningiomas (ONSM). We retrospectively identified patients with ONSM treated with CK between January 2020 and January 2024 from the Database of Chinese Neuro-Ophthalmic Diseases. CK was delivered at 23–25 Gy in 5 fractions. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and visual field mean deviation (VF MD) were assessed before treatment and at the final follow-up, with a median visual follow-up of 36 months (range, 26–64 months). Tumor volume and CK-related complications were also evaluated. Twenty patients (22 affected eyes; 2 with bilateral involvement) were included. Treatment success was achieved in 90.9% (20/22) of eyes, including improvement in 59.1% (13/22) and stable visual function in 31.8% (7/22), whereas 9.1% (2/22) worsened. Among the 12 eyes with available VF MD data, 91.7% (11/12) improved and 8.3% (1/12) worsened. Spearman correlation analysis revealed that poorer baseline BCVA (r = 0.457, p = 0.032) and a longer interval from onset to CK (r = 0.450, p = 0.036) were associated with poorer visual outcomes, whereas age and tumor volume were not significantly associated with visual changes (p > 0.05). MRI follow-up was available for 13 patients (14 eyes), with tumor control achieved in all 14 eyes. No serious treatment-related complications were observed. CK hypofractionated radiosurgery may preserve and improve visual function in ONSM, providing a potentially safe and effective treatment option.

title: Perceived Stress and Ocular Surface Symptoms: A Survey-Based Study of Medical Students

payload.title: Perceived Stress and Ocular Surface Symptoms: A Survey-Based Study of Medical Students
payload.abstract: Background: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of symptomatic dry eye among medical students and identify associated demographic and psychological factors. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among medical students enrolled at Jordanian universities during September 2025. Participants completed a structured electronic questionnaire including demographic and lifestyle characteristics, the validated Perceived Stress Scale-10 (PSS-10), and the validated Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with severe symptomatic dry eye. Results: A total of 311 medical students participated. The mean OSDI score was 34.84 ± 18.18, with 54.7% classified as having severe symptomatic dry eye. In multivariable logistic regression, perceived stress was associated with severe symptomatic dry eye after adjustment for measured covariates (adjusted OR = 1.056, 95% CI: 1.015–1.098, p = 0.007). Higher perceived stress was also associated with greater symptom severity (p = 0.001) and higher OSDI scores after adjustment (p = 0.010). Conclusions: Symptomatic dry eye symptoms were highly prevalent among medical students, and perceived stress was associated with greater symptom burden and severity after adjustment for measured covariates. These findings highlight the potential relevance of stress-related factors to ocular symptoms among medical students and encourage further investigation.

title: Long-Term Outcomes and Safety of Non-Cyclodialytic, Bleb-Independent Surgical Enhancement of Uveoscleral Outflow in Open-Angle Glaucoma, with Evaluation of the Role of Conjunctival Lymphatic Vessels in Suprachoroidal Drainage

payload.title: Long-Term Outcomes and Safety of Non-Cyclodialytic, Bleb-Independent Surgical Enhancement of Uveoscleral Outflow in Open-Angle Glaucoma, with Evaluation of the Role of Conjunctival Lymphatic Vessels in Suprachoroidal Drainage
payload.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate long-term outcomes and safety of non-cyclodialytic, bleb-independent surgical enhancement of uveoscleral outflow for intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction in open-angle glaucoma (OAG), and to assess the role of conjunctival lymphatic vessels (CLVs) in suprachoroidal drainage. Methods: In this single-center consecutive case series, 70 eyes of 63 patients (mean age 75.0 years; 70% female) with moderate-to-severe OAG underwent uveoscleral outflow enhancement. Twenty-two eyes had standalone surgery; 48 eyes had combined phacoemulsification with glaucoma surgery. Mean follow-up was 24.1 months (range 5.3–60.4). Primary outcomes were IOP reduction and surgical success by Kaplan–Meier analysis (sustained failure: IOP > 18 mmHg or < 20% reduction from baseline at two consecutive available postoperative visits, excluding day 1). CLVs were assessed by slit-lamp and OCT at 11 time points over 36 months. Mixed-effects models with random intercept per eye were used for repeated measurements. Logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors evaluated predictors of CLV visibility. Results: Baseline IOP of 28.8 ± 8.4 mmHg decreased to 12.3 ± 4.5 mmHg at 1 month (54.5% reduction) and 14.5 ± 2.5 mmHg at 36 months (46.2% reduction, n = 22). Medications decreased from 2.77 ± 0.94 to 1.36 ± 1.09 at 36 months. Overall surgical survival was 91.4% at 1 month, 82.0% at 12 months, and 74.1% at 36 months. Fifteen eyes (21.4%) met sustained failure criteria (standalone surgery group: eight, combined surgery group: seven; and log-rank p = 0.038). The combined surgery group showed higher survival at 36 months (82.6% vs. 58.5%), but the difference did not reach significance. CLVs were detected in 51.4% by slit-lamp and 96.4% by OCT, peaking at 1 month. Before surgery, CLVs were not detected on OCT in any eye. Time was a significant negative predictor of CLV visibility on both slit-lamp (OR 0.953/month, p = 0.046) and OCT (OR 0.935/month, p = 0.003), without independent association with IOP or medication burden, suggesting that CLVs facilitate suprachoroidal drainage as a structural mechanism rather than a reactive response to IOP changes. Conclusions: Non-cyclodialytic, bleb-independent uveoscleral outflow enhancement provides sustained IOP reduction with favorable safety. CLVs, nearly universally detected by OCT after surgery, appear to contribute to suprachoroidal drainage. Combined surgery showed a trend toward greater surgical success than standalone procedures.

title: Effects of Traditional Chinese Medicine for Prevention and Management of Dry Eye Disease: A Systematic Review, Network Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression of Randomized Controlled Trials

payload.title: Effects of Traditional Chinese Medicine for Prevention and Management of Dry Eye Disease: A Systematic Review, Network Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression of Randomized Controlled Trials
payload.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent ocular surface disorder with diverse clinical presentations, yet the comparative efficacy of various Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations remains unclear. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated the comparative effects and baseline response relationships of TCM classes for DED across 33 randomized controlled trials retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and CNKI. Primary outcomes included Schirmer I test (SIT), tear film break-up time (TBUT), and corneal fluorescein staining (FL). Random-effects models estimated weighted mean differences (WMD) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs); for FL, which was measured on heterogeneous grading scales and standardized mean differences (SMD) were used. TCM classes exhibited outcome-specific profiles: Yin–Kidney (YK) and Qi–Yin Support (QYS) produced the greatest improvements in SIT versus standard care (YK: WMD 2.56, 95% CrI 0.25 to 4.86; QYS: WMD 5.32, 95% CrI 0.63 to 10.06) and significantly improved TBUT (YK: WMD 2.04, 95% CrI 1.12 to 2.89; YM: WMD 2.49, 95% CrI 0.64 to 4.37). YK demonstrated the greatest FL reduction (SMD −0.37, 95% CrI −0.71 to 0.00), followed by Liver–Spleen Regulating (SMD −0.30, 95% CrI −0.99 to 0.39). Meta-regression revealed that patients with more severe baseline deficits in tear secretion (lower SIT) and more extensive ocular-surface damage (higher FL) achieved greater clinical improvements, whereas baseline of TBUT did not significantly moderate treatment response. Overall, TCM serves as an effective adjunctive therapy for DED, with selection guided by clinical pattern and target outcomes.

title: Showing versus doing: Teaching by demonstration

payload.title: Showing versus doing: Teaching by demonstration
payload.abstract: People often learn from others' demonstrations, and classic inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) algorithms have brought us closer to realizing this capacity in machines. In contrast, teaching by demonstration has been less well studied computationally. Here, we develop a novel Bayesian model for teaching by demonstration. Stark differences arise when demonstrators are intentionally teaching a task versus simply performing a task. In two experiments, we show that human participants systematically modify their teaching behavior consistent with the predictions of our model. Further, we show that even standard IRL algorithms benefit when learning from behaviors that are intentionally pedagogical. We conclude by discussing IRL algorithms that can take advantage of intentional pedagogy.

Autonomous Quantum Measurement with Agentic AI

payload.title: Autonomous Quantum Measurement with Agentic AI
payload.abstract: Quantum materials exhibit diverse electronic and functional phenomena, but their characterization requires extensive experimental expertise, iterative decision-making and accumulated laboratory knowledge that is difficult to document and transfer. Here we introduce Quantum Agent (QUANTA), an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for autonomous quantum-materials characterization. Using a widely adopted Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS) as an experimental platform, QUANTA combines retrieval augmentation using scientific literature, experimental protocols and prior measurements with specialized agents for experimental planning, troubleshooting, and data interpretation. A separate deterministic control layer validates instrument actions. Guided by incoming data, QUANTA evaluates measurement quality, revises experimental plans and selects subsequent measurements. We demonstrate these capabilities through transport measurements of the topological Weyl semimetal TaP, as well as investigations of nonlinear responses in magnetic material Co2MnGa. These results establish QUANTA as a generalizable framework for evidence-driven, safeguarded and closed-loop quantum-materials characterization.

title: Discovery of Diverse and Realistic Financial Tail-Risk Using Generative Flow Networks

payload.title: Discovery of Diverse and Realistic Financial Tail-Risk Using Generative Flow Networks
payload.abstract: Accurate modeling of rare, high-impact financial events is essential for robust risk management. Sampling-based techniques such as Sequential Markov Chain Monte Carlo (SMCMC) generate diverse scenarios but inefficiently explore high-risk regions, while Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) converges on narrow sets of scenarios, limiting diversity. We present GRID, which uses Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) -- samplers that draw objects in proportion to a reward -- to systematically generate diverse and realistic financial tail-risk scenarios. Building on continuous GFlowNets, GRID introduces a flexible mixture-policy architecture with variable-specific distribution families for high-dimensional, sequential macro-financial data, together with plausibility constraints that keep generated trajectories realistic. A central practical advantage is robustness to reward-proxy imperfection: because GFlowNets sample proportionally rather than maximize, they remain broadly exploratory even when the oracle's out-of-sample accuracy is low -- an unavoidable reality in financial forecasting. On three real-world crises, GRID improves scenario diversity, realism, and tail-risk coverage over RL and MCMC baselines, and ablations over oracle architectures and distribution families yield practical insights into continuous GFlowNet behavior under noisy rewards.

title: What to randomize matters: a controlled study of volume, axis and representation in low-data molecular generation

payload.title: What to randomize matters: a controlled study of volume, axis and representation in low-data molecular generation
payload.abstract: Chemical language models can struggle to generate new molecules when trained on small datasets, where a model may reproduce training examples rather than learn a useful generative distribution. Randomized SMILES augmentation varies atom traversal, whereas Sequential Attachment-based Fragment Embedding (SAFE) also allows the order of fragment blocks to vary. How these distinct sources of representational variation affect low-data molecular generation has not been clearly studied. Here, using 1,000 seed molecules to train an autoregressive sequence model, we compare canonical SAFE with randomized SAFE at increasing corpus sizes, isolate atom-order and fragment-order axes of SAFE randomization, and compare fully randomized SAFE with randomized SMILES at molecule-by-molecule matched training corpora. Three findings emerge. First, randomization of SAFE alone raises the genuine yield of novel molecules more than 450-fold, turning a model that merely reproduces its training set into a practical molecular generator. Second, the two axes of randomization act jointly rather than additively: atom order alone reaches a tenth, and fragment order alone a seventh, of the genuine yield obtained when both vary, which is four times their combined contribution. Third, at matched corpus size and compute, randomized SAFE delivers 2.8 times the genuine yield of randomized SMILES. Welch tests with Games-Howell post-hoc comparisons resolve every difference on the primary outcomes. In the low-data regime, thus, what one randomizes rather than only how much determines whether augmentation produces new molecules or merely new spellings of the training set.

title: Discovering Jailbreaks via Curriculum of Models

payload.title: Discovering Jailbreaks via Curriculum of Models
payload.abstract: Automated jailbreak discovery aims to find prompts that elicit prohibited behaviors from safety-trained language models, helping developers identify vulnerabilities before deployment. One class of approaches uses reinforcement learning to train an investigator model to generate prompts that elicit a specified behavior from a target model. However, training directly against a safety-trained target is difficult because nearly all prompts are refused, leaving the investigator with a sparse reward signal. Prior work addresses this with the propensity bound (PRBO), a proxy reward estimated by sampling responses from a more compliant target, and then adjusting for how likely those responses would have been under the original target. We introduce Curriculum of Models (CoM), an alternative method that trains the investigator against a sequence of modified versions of the target, progressing gradually from a version that readily exhibits the specified behavior to the original target. For jailbreak discovery, training begins against a target version that rarely refuses harmful requests, and advances to the next, harder version once the investigator reliably elicits the behavior from the current one. We evaluate CoM on elicitation tasks involving CBRN materials, explosives, and illicit drugs, using two open-weight targets, gemma-4-31b-it and gpt-oss-120b. We compare against PRBO and direct training on the original target without a curriculum. When the investigator is trained to elicit a single behavior, CoM finds successful jailbreaks more reliably than either baseline. When trained on multiple behaviors simultaneously, the CoM-trained investigator can elicit held-out behaviors, though PRBO-trained investigators achieve higher success rates. Our results suggest that a simple curriculum over target models offers a promising approach for addressing sparse rewards in rare-behavior elicitation.

title: Evaluating Visual Realism of AI-Generated Videos with Eye Tracking

payload.title: Evaluating Visual Realism of AI-Generated Videos with Eye Tracking
payload.abstract: Human evaluation of AI-generated videos has so far relied on explicit human feedback, such as judgments or ratings. While these signals capture the conclusions viewers reach, they fail to offer insights into the perception that leads to them. This paper investigates eye tracking as a complementary human evaluation signal for AI-generated videos. We conducted two Visual Turing Test (VTT) experiments with a total of 90 participants on videos generated by latest generative models, in which participants watched each video twice and then gave their feedback. Across the experiments, we collected 4,286 valid eye-tracking trials on 438 videos. Our analysis indicates that gaze patterns offer informative evaluation signals that align with explicit human feedback. Building on the findings, we propose the first computational method GazeEval to predict the perceived visual realism of AI-generated videos from eye-tracking data. It achieves 71.3% accuracy in prediction, providing evidence that eye tracking data carries informative signals about how people evaluate a video. We release the study data to support further research on eye tracking for evaluating AI-generated video.

title: UnEZ: A Fully Unsupervised Self-Templating Neural Network for Redshift and Line Strength Estimation

payload.title: UnEZ: A Fully Unsupervised Self-Templating Neural Network for Redshift and Line Strength Estimation
payload.abstract: As spectroscopic surveys grow, estimating galaxy properties such as metallicity, star formation rate, and redshift becomes computationally cumbersome. Methods of estimating such properties rely on template spectra or curated redshift catalogs, which fail to represent the diversity of objects seen in large-scale surveys. We present UnEZ, a fully unsupervised, physics-informed machine learning model that can predict spectroscopic redshifts and line strengths with no prior redshift or line strength labels. An encoder predicts emission and absorption line amplitudes/widths, and a fixed deterministic decoder constructs a unique template, estimated redshift, redshift confidence curve, and spectral model. UnEZ was tested on the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Data Release 18 due to its large dataset and thoroughly vetted redshift catalog which serves as an independent benchmark. Despite the lack of templates, line strength labels, or redshift labels, UnEZ's performance competes with modern redshift estimation algorithms. At SNR > 10, UnEZ achieves an outlier fraction of 0.459% and a normalized median absolute deviation (NMAD) of $1.237 \times 10^{-4}$. At SNR > 3, UnEZ achieves an outlier fraction of 3.89% and an NMAD of $1.471 \times 10^{-4}$. Furthermore, we demonstrate how UnEZ's line strength and redshift predictions can be utilized for various purposes such as constructing template spectra required in traditional redshift estimation algorithms. UnEZ illustrates how a fully unsupervised neural network can allow redshift, among other galaxy properties, to emerge naturally from the spectra themselves, providing a template-free, label-free approach that scales to the demands of future surveys.

title: Causal Attention on CPU: A Cache-Aware and Load-Balanced Scheduling Kernel for Prefill

payload.title: Causal Attention on CPU: A Cache-Aware and Load-Balanced Scheduling Kernel for Prefill
payload.abstract: Agentic AI drives significant productivity gains across diverse domains, but concurrent long-context prefills from multiple agents can saturate GPU compute resources. Although CPUs offer a viable alternative, existing CPU attention kernels fall short in adapting to multi-tier cache hierarchies and lack effective thread scheduling. To address this, we introduce CACPU, a high-performance attention kernel featuring tiered cache blocking and an in-kernel task dispatching mechanism designed for causal full-sequence prefilling. CACPU achieves up to a 2.01x speedup over PyTorch SDPA, FlexAttention, and SGLang attention kernels. Integrated into SGLang, it reduces Time to First Token (TTFT) of Llama-3.1-8B by up to 1.74x while preserving model accuracy.

title: Pinpointing Pivot Points: The DECIDE Framework for Data Analysis Decision Importances

payload.title: Pinpointing Pivot Points: The DECIDE Framework for Data Analysis Decision Importances
payload.abstract: Human judgment calls made throughout the data science life cycle can change the conclusions drawn from data. Independent analysts often make different choices when given the same data, leading to often unacceptable variations in results and contributing to the ongoing reproducibility crisis across scientific disciplines. The rapid adoption of agentic tools threatens to amplify this crisis. Several approaches have been developed to address this variation by following the same strategy: repeating an analysis under different combinations of analytical decisions and inspecting the distribution of outcomes. Examples include multiverse analysis, specification curve analysis, and vibration of effects. More broadly, the Predictability-Computability-Stability (PCS) framework assesses how documented judgment calls across the data science life cycle affect conclusions, with predictability serving as a reality-check that a model captures signal. Each of these approaches results in a "multiverse" object. While the distribution of outcomes reflects the overall variability of conclusions, estimating the influence of each individual decision requires additional tools. A common heuristic is to train a model to predict the outcome from these decisions and treat its coefficients or feature importances as proxies for each decision's influence. Although this strategy may work in certain cases, it assumes the model is correctly specified and accurately predicts the outcome, which we show is not always the case.
